title.zh: 卷93 恩幸:王叡 王仲興 寇猛 趙修 茹皓 趙邕 侯剛等
title.en: Volume 93: Favorites of Nobles - Wang Rui, Wang Zhongxing, Kou Meng, Zhao Xiu, Ru Hao, Zhao Yong, Hou Gang, and others
title.raw: 卷93 恩幸:王叡 王仲興 寇猛 趙修 茹皓 趙邕 侯剛等 Volume 93: Favorites of Nobles - Wang Rui, Wang Zhongxing, Kou Meng, Zhao Xiu, Ru Hao, Zhao Yong, Hou Gang, and others

sentences.zh: 王叡 王仲興 寇猛 趙脩 茹晧 趙邕 侯剛 鄭儼 徐紇

translations.literal: Wang Rui, Wang Zhongxing, Kou Meng, Zhao Xiu, Ru Hao, Zhao Yong, Hou Gang, Zheng Yan, and Xu He.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui, Wang Zhongxing, Kou Meng, Zhao Xiu, Ru Hao, Zhao Yong, Hou Gang, Zheng Yan, and Xu He.

sentences.zh: 夫令色巧言，矯情飾貌，邀眄睞之利，射咳唾之私，此蓋苟進之常也。

translations.literal: Those who cultivate a flattering face and clever words, distort their feelings and adorn their appearance, and seek advantage from glances and private favor are all ordinary cases of advancement by questionable means.
translations.idiomatic: Those who cultivate a flattering face and clever words, distort their feelings and ornament their appearance, and angle for advantage through a glance or a favor are only pursuing advancement by improper means.

sentences.zh: 故甚者刑身瀹子，其次舐痔嘗癰，況乃散金秦貨，輸錢漢爵，又何怪哉？

translations.literal: The worst of them would even torture their own bodies and sacrifice their children; the next would lick boils and taste sores. Let alone scattering gold like Qin wares and paying money for Han titles, what is there to wonder at?
translations.idiomatic: The worst would go so far as to maim themselves and sacrifice their children; the next would lick boils and taste sores. If they could even scatter gold or buy titles with cash, what is there to be astonished at?

sentences.zh: 若夫地窮尊貴，嗜欲所攻，聖達其猶病諸，中庸固不能免。

translations.literal: As for those who stand at the summit of rank and power and are attacked by desire, even the sages and the accomplished still suffer from it; the middling and ordinary, of course, cannot escape.
translations.idiomatic: When one has reached the height of honor and power, desire still makes its attack. Even sages and masters are afflicted by it, and the moderate and ordinary certainly cannot avoid it.

sentences.zh: 男女性態，其揆斯一，二代之亡，皆是物也。

translations.literal: Male and female conduct is measured by the same standard; the fall of the two dynasties alike came from these things.
translations.idiomatic: Male and female conduct follow the same pattern, and the ruin of the two dynasties alike came from such matters.

sentences.zh: 據天下之圖，持海內之命，顧指如意，高下在心，此乃夏桀、殷紂喪二邦，秦母、呂雉穢兩國也。

translations.literal: To grasp the map of the realm and hold the fate of all under heaven, to have one's nod and gesture produce whatever one wishes, and to set high and low entirely at one's own heart: this is how Xia Jie and Yin Zhou lost their two states, and how Qin's mother and Empress Lü disgraced the two countries.
translations.idiomatic: When one holds the realm's map and the fate of all under heaven, with every nod and gesture made to produce what one wants and rank fixed by one's own will, that is how Xia Jie and Yin Zhou lost their two kingdoms and how Qin's mother and Empress Lü sullied theirs.

sentences.zh: 魏世，王叡幸太和之初，鄭儼寵孝昌之季，主幼於前，君稚於後，乘間宣淫，殆無忌畏，樹列朋黨，蔽塞天聰。

translations.literal: In Wei times, Wang Rui was favored at the start of the Taihe era, and Zheng Yan at the end of Xiaochang. With child rulers before and after them, they took advantage of the openings to give free rein to lust, almost without fear or restraint, building cliques and blocking the ruler's divine hearing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wei dynasty, Wang Rui won favor at the start of Taihe and Zheng Yan at the end of Xiaochang. With child rulers before and after them, they exploited the gaps to indulge lust almost without fear, built cliques, and shut out the ruler's enlightened hearing.

sentences.zh: 高祖明聖外彰，人神繫仰，御之有術，宗社弗墜。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao's enlightened sagacity shone abroad, and people and spirits alike looked up to him; he ruled with skill, and the ancestral shrine did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao's enlightened virtue shone everywhere, and both people and spirits looked up to him. He governed with skill, and the state did not fall.

sentences.zh: 肅宗不言垂拱，潛濟罕方，六合淆然，至於隕覆。

translations.literal: Emperor Su, by silently sitting with hands folded, had few hidden methods of rescue; the whole world became confused and came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Su ruled in silent repose, yet his hidden measures were few, and the whole realm fell into confusion and ruin.

sentences.zh: 且承顏色，竊光寵，勢等秋風，氣同夏日，亦何世而不有哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, those who curry favor with a smiling face and secretly bask in grace have power like the autumn wind and spirit like the summer sun; in what age have they not existed?
translations.idiomatic: Those who court favor with a smile and secretly share in grace have power as fleeting as autumn wind and a temperament as hot as summer sun. In what age have they ever been absent?

sentences.zh: 此周旦所以誡其朋，詩人是為疾羣小也。

translations.literal: This is why Zhou Dan warned his companions, and why the poets hated the petty ones.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the Duke of Zhou warned his companions and why the poets denounced the petty men.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，王、車之徒，雖云幸念，皆宣力夷險，誠效兼存，未如趙脩等出於近習趨走之地，坐擅威刑，勢傾都鄙，得之非道，君子所以賤之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizong's reign, the likes of Wang and Che, though said to be favored and remembered, all exerted themselves in rough and easy places, with loyalty and service both preserved; they were not like Zhao Xiu and the rest, who rose from the circle of close attendants and runners, sat there monopolizing authority and punishment, and whose power overmatched city and countryside. To obtain it by such means is not the proper way, and gentlemen therefore despise it.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Taizong's reign, the likes of Wang and Che, though favored, still threw themselves into hard and easy tasks alike, preserving both loyalty and service. They were nothing like Zhao Xiu and the others, who rose from the circle of close attendants and runners, sat there monopolizing power and punishment, and whose influence overwhelmed town and countryside. To gain power that way is not the proper path, and gentlemen despise it.

sentences.zh: 書其變態，備禍福之由焉。

translations.literal: I record their changes and dispositions, to make clear the causes of misfortune and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: I record their turns and changes so as to show the causes of fortune and disaster.

sentences.zh: 王叡，字洛誠，自云太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Rui, courtesy name Luocheng, said that he was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui, courtesy name Luocheng, said himself to be from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 六世祖橫，張軌參軍。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Heng served as an assistant officer to Zhang Gui.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Heng served as a military aide to Zhang Gui.

sentences.zh: 晉亂，子孫因居於武威姑臧。

translations.literal: When Jin fell into disorder, his descendants therefore settled in Guzang of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin fell into chaos, the descendants settled in Guzang in Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 父橋，字法生，解天文卜筮。

translations.literal: His father Qiao, courtesy name Fasheng, understood astronomy and divination.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiao, courtesy name Fasheng, understood astronomy and divination.

sentences.zh: 涼州平，入京，家貧，以術自給。

translations.literal: When Liangzhou was pacified, he entered the capital; because the family was poor, he supported himself by his skill.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzhou was pacified, he entered the capital, and because the family was poor, he made his living by his skills.

sentences.zh: 歷仕終於侍御中散。

translations.literal: He served in various posts and ended as Attendant Censor Zhongsan.
translations.idiomatic: He served in a series of posts and ended as Attendant Censor Zhongsan.

sentences.zh: 天安初卒，贈平遠將軍、涼州刺史、顯美侯，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Tian'an and was posthumously granted the titles General of Far Pacification, Inspector of Liangzhou, and Marquis of Xianmei, with the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the start of Tian'an and was posthumously named General of Far Pacification, Inspector of Liangzhou, and Marquis of Xianmei, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 叡少傳父業，而姿貌偉麗。

translations.literal: Rui learned his father's craft from youth and had a grand and handsome bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Rui learned his father's craft when young and had a grand, handsome appearance.

sentences.zh: 恭宗之在東宮，見而奇之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong was in the Eastern Palace, he saw him and found him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong was in the Eastern Palace, he saw him and thought him remarkable.

sentences.zh: 興安初，擢為太卜中散，稍遷為令，領太史。

translations.literal: At the start of Xing'an, he was promoted to Taibu Zhongsan, then gradually advanced to Ling and given concurrent charge of the Grand Astrologer Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xing'an, he was promoted to Taibu Zhongsan, then advanced to head the bureau and take charge of the Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 承明元年，文明太后臨朝，叡因緣見幸，超遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengming, when the Civilizing Empress Dowager was conducting the court, Rui gained favor through connections and was leap-promoted to Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chengming, when the Civilizing Empress Dowager was ruling the court, Rui won favor through connections and was rapidly promoted to Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 俄而為散騎常侍、侍中、吏部尚書，賜爵太原公。

translations.literal: Soon he became Palace Attendant, Palace Gentleman, and Minister of Civil Appointments, and was granted the title Duke of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he became Palace Attendant, Palace Gentleman, and Minister of Civil Appointments, and was granted the title Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 於是內參機密，外豫政事，愛寵日隆，朝士懾憚焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter he took part in the state's secret affairs within court and in government business outside it, and his favor and affection grew by the day; the court officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he was admitted to the state's secrets inside court and to its affairs outside it, and his favor grew daily; the court officials feared and deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，高祖及文明太后率百僚與諸方客臨虎圈，有逸虎登門閣道，幾至御座。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, Emperor Gao and the Civilizing Empress Dowager led the hundred officials and visiting envoys from all directions to the tiger enclosure. A loose tiger climbed the gate corridor and nearly reached the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe, Emperor Gao and the Civilizing Empress Dowager led the hundred officials and envoys from many states to the tiger enclosure, where a loose tiger climbed the gate corridor and nearly reached the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 左右侍御皆驚靡，叡獨執戟禦之，虎乃退去，故親任轉重。

translations.literal: The attendants on the left and right were all alarmed and fled, but Rui alone held his halberd and warded it off, whereupon the tiger retreated, so his personal trust became even greater.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants on both sides were all thrown into panic, but Rui alone held his halberd and drove it back, and the tiger withdrew. His favor and trust therefore grew even greater.

sentences.zh: 三年春，詔叡與東陽王丕同入八議，永受復除。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, an edict ordered Rui and Prince Pi of Dongyang to enter the Eight Deliberations together and enjoy perpetual exemption from taxes and service.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year, an edict ordered Rui and Prince Pi of Dongyang to be included in the Eight Deliberations and granted permanent exemption from taxes and service.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷尚書令，封爵中山王，加鎮東大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Shangshu Ling, enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongshan, and added as Great General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Shangshu Ling, enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongshan, and given the added title of Great General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 置王官二十二人，中書侍郎鄭羲為傅，郎中令以下皆當時名士。

translations.literal: Twenty-two royal attendants were appointed; Zhongshu Shilang Zheng Xi was made tutor, and everyone from the Langzhong Ling down was a famous man of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two palace officers were appointed; Zhongshu Shilang Zheng Xi served as tutor, and everyone from the Langzhong Ling downward was a noted man of the day.

sentences.zh: 又拜叡妻丁氏為妃。

translations.literal: Rui's wife, Lady Ding, was also appointed as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's wife, Lady Ding, was also appointed as a consort.

sentences.zh: 及沙門法秀謀逆，事發，多所牽引。

translations.literal: When the monk Faxiu plotted rebellion and the matter came to light, many people were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: When the monk Faxiu plotted rebellion and the affair was exposed, many people were dragged in.

sentences.zh: 叡曰：「與其殺不辜，寧赦有罪。

translations.literal: Rui said: 'Rather than kill the innocent, it is better to pardon the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, 'Rather than kill the innocent, it is better to pardon the guilty.

sentences.zh: 宜梟斬首惡，餘從疑赦，不亦善乎？

translations.literal: It would be proper to behead the chief offenders and pardon the rest on doubtful grounds; would that not be good?
translations.idiomatic: It would be best to behead the chief offenders and pardon the rest where there is doubt. Would that not be good?

sentences.zh: 」高祖從之，得免者千餘人。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice, and more than a thousand people were spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice, and more than a thousand people were spared.

sentences.zh: 叡出入帷幄，太后密賜珍玩繒綵，人莫能知，率常以夜帷車載往，閹官防致，前後巨萬，不可勝數，加以田園、奴婢、牛馬、雜畜，並盡良美。

translations.literal: Rui came and went within the imperial curtains. The empress dowager secretly bestowed on him rare playthings and silks, and no one knew of it; they were usually sent at night in curtained carts and delivered through eunuchs. The amounts over time reached into the tens of thousands and could not be counted. In addition, he was given fields and gardens, slaves, cattle, horses, and other livestock, all of them fine and excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Rui moved freely in and out of the imperial curtains. The empress dowager secretly gave him rare playthings and silks, unknown to anyone else; they were usually conveyed at night in curtained carts and delivered through eunuchs. Over time the gifts amounted to tens of thousands and could not be counted. He also received fields, gardens, slaves, cattle, horses, and other livestock, all of them the best quality.

sentences.zh: 大臣及左右因是以受賚錫，外示不私，所費又以萬計。

translations.literal: The great ministers and his attendants also received gifts on account of this, so outwardly it appeared that he was not keeping anything for himself, though the expenditures again ran into the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers and his attendants also received gifts because of it, so that outwardly it seemed he was not keeping anything for himself, though the outlay again ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 及疾病，高祖、太后每親視疾，侍官省問，相望於道。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, Emperor Gao and the empress dowager would often personally visit him, and attendants and officials came and went in a stream along the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, Emperor Gao and the empress dowager repeatedly came in person to ask after him, and attendants and officials were constantly moving back and forth along the road.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，上疏曰：

translations.literal: When his illness became grave, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave, he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞忠於事君者，節義著於臨終；

translations.literal: I have heard that those who are loyal in serving their ruler make their sense of duty and righteousness evident at the end of life;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who are loyal in serving their ruler make their integrity and righteousness clear at the end of life;

sentences.zh: 孝於奉親者，淳誠表於垂沒。

translations.literal: and those who are filial in serving their parents show their pure sincerity as death approaches.
translations.idiomatic: and those who are filial in serving their parents show their pure sincerity as death draws near.

sentences.zh: 故孔明卒軍，不忘全蜀之計；

translations.literal: Thus Kong Ming died while with the army and did not forget the plan to preserve Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Kong Ming died in command of the army and never forgot the plan to preserve Shu;

sentences.zh: 曾參疾甚，情存善言之益。

translations.literal: and when Zeng Shen was gravely ill, his feelings still held to the benefit of good words.
translations.idiomatic: and when Zeng Shen was gravely ill, his thoughts still rested on the value of good counsel.

sentences.zh: 雖則庸昧，敢忘景行。

translations.literal: Though I am dull and ignorant, how could I dare forget such lofty conduct?
translations.idiomatic: Though I am dull and ignorant, how could I dare forget such noble conduct?

sentences.zh: 臣荷天地覆載之恩，蒙大造生成之德，漸風訓於華年，服道教於弱冠。

translations.literal: I have borne the grace of heaven and earth's covering and carrying, and received the great virtue by which I was brought forth and nurtured; in my youthful years I gradually came under instruction and took on the teachings of the Way before reaching twenty.
translations.idiomatic: I have borne the grace of heaven and earth's covering and sustaining, and received the great virtue by which I was brought forth and nurtured; in my youth I was gradually shaped by instruction and embraced the teachings of the Way before I was twenty.

sentences.zh: 濯纓清朝，垂周三紀，受先帝非分之眷，叨陛下殊常之寵。

translations.literal: I have washed my sash in the pure court for nearly three cycles, receiving from the late emperor favor beyond my due and from Your Majesty extraordinary grace.
translations.idiomatic: I have washed my sash in the pure court for nearly three decades, receiving from the former emperor favor beyond my due and from Your Majesty extraordinary grace.

sentences.zh: 遂乃齊跡功舊，內侍幃幄，爵列諸王，位班上等，從容聞道，與知國政。

translations.literal: Thus I came to match the traces of former meritorious men, serve within the curtains at court, stand in rank among the princes, occupy the upper tier of office, hear the Way at leisure, and share knowledge of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I came to stand beside former meritorious men, serving within the curtains at court, ranked among the princes, placed in the upper tier of office, hearing the Way at leisure, and sharing in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 誠思竭盡力命，以報所受，不謂事與心違，忽嬰重疾。

translations.literal: I truly hoped to exhaust my strength and life in repayment for what I had received, but unexpectedly matters ran against my wishes and I was suddenly stricken with a grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: I truly hoped to spend my strength and life in repayment for what I had received, but events went against my wishes and I was suddenly stricken with a grave illness.

sentences.zh: 每屈輿駕親臨問之，榮洽生平，惠流身後，犬馬之誠，銜佩罔極。

translations.literal: Whenever Your Majesty bent the carriage and came in person to inquire after me, the honor I have enjoyed in life and the favor that will flow after death are beyond my power to repay; I bear them in loyal gratitude without end.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Your Majesty bent the carriage to come in person and inquire after me, the honor I have enjoyed in life and the favor that will flow after death are beyond my power to repay; I bear them with loyal gratitude beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 今所病遂篤，慮必不起，延首闕庭，鯁戀終日。

translations.literal: Now my illness has grown severe, and I fear I will not recover; I keep stretching my neck toward the palace court, heavy with longing all day long.
translations.idiomatic: Now my illness has grown severe, and I fear I will not recover. I keep stretching my neck toward the palace court, weighed down with longing all day long.

sentences.zh: 仰恃皇造宿眷之隆，敢陳愚昧管窺之見。

translations.literal: Relying on the greatness of the imperial grace and your long-standing favor, I venture to present my foolish, narrow view.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on the greatness of the imperial grace and your long-standing favor, I venture to present this foolish, narrow view of mine.

sentences.zh: 臣聞為治之要，其略有五：一者慎刑罰，二者任賢能，三者親忠信，四者遠讒佞，五者行黜陟。

translations.literal: I have heard that the essentials of good governance are five: first, be careful with punishments; second, employ the worthy and capable; third, draw near to the loyal and trustworthy; fourth, keep away from slanderers and flatterers; fifth, carry out promotion and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the essentials of good governance are five: first, be careful with punishments; second, employ the worthy and capable; third, draw near to the loyal and trustworthy; fourth, keep away from slanderers and flatterers; fifth, carry out promotion and demotion.

sentences.zh: 夫刑罰明則姦宄息，賢能用則功績著，親忠信則視聽審，遠讒佞則疑間絕，黜陟行則貪叨改。

translations.literal: When punishments are clear, evil deeds stop; when the worthy and capable are employed, achievements become manifest; when the loyal and trustworthy are near, what the ruler sees and hears is reliable; when slanderers and flatterers are kept away, suspicion and estrangement end; when promotions and demotions are carried out, greed and indolence are corrected.
translations.idiomatic: When punishments are clear, evil deeds cease; when the worthy and capable are employed, achievements become visible; when the loyal and trustworthy are kept close, what the ruler sees and hears is dependable; when slanderers and flatterers are kept away, suspicion and estrangement disappear; and when promotions and demotions are properly carried out, greed and laxity are corrected.

sentences.zh: 是以欽恤惟刑，載在唐典；

translations.literal: For this reason, careful and compassionate punishment is recorded in the Tang canons;
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, careful and compassionate punishment is recorded in the Tang canons;

sentences.zh: 知人則哲，唯帝所難。

translations.literal: To know people and thus be wise is what even an emperor finds difficult.
translations.idiomatic: To know people and thus be wise is what even an emperor finds difficult.

sentences.zh: 周書垂好德之文，漢史列防姦之論，考省幽明，先王大典。

translations.literal: The Book of Zhou sets forth texts praising virtue; the Han histories arrange discussions on guarding against corruption. Together they examine the hidden and the manifest, and they are the great ordinances of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Zhou sets forth texts praising virtue, and the Han histories present arguments for guarding against corruption. They examine both the hidden and the manifest, and they are the great ordinances of the former kings.

sentences.zh: 又八表既廣，遠近事殊，撫荒裔宜待之以寬信，綏華甸宜惠之以明簡。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the outer reaches are broad and affairs near and far differ, those who govern the frontier wastes should treat them with generosity and trust, while those who pacify the civilized regions should favor them with clear simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the outer reaches are so broad and the affairs of near and far differ, those who govern the frontier wastes should treat them with generosity and trust, while those who pacify the civilized regions should favor them with clear simplicity.

sentences.zh: 哀恤孤獨，賑施困窮，錄功舊，赦小罪，輕徭役，薄賦斂，修福業，禁淫祀。

translations.literal: Show compassion for the widowed and solitary, relieve the distressed and poor, record the merits of old officials, pardon small offenses, lighten labor service, reduce taxes and levies, cultivate meritorious works, and prohibit licentious sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Show compassion for the widowed and solitary, relieve the distressed and poor, record the merits of old officials, pardon small offenses, lighten labor service, reduce taxes and levies, cultivate meritorious works, and prohibit licentious sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 願聽政餘暇，賜垂覽察。

translations.literal: I hope that when you have leisure from affairs of state, you will condescend to inspect this.
translations.idiomatic: I hope that when you have leisure from affairs of state, you will condescend to inspect this.

sentences.zh: 使子囊之誠，重申於當世；

translations.literal: So that the sincerity of Ziniang may be once again made manifest in the present age;
translations.idiomatic: So that the sincerity of Ziniang may once again be made manifest in the present age;

sentences.zh: 將墜之志，獲用於明時。

translations.literal: And the ambition on the verge of collapse may yet be put to use in an enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: And the ambition on the verge of collapse may yet be put to use in an enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，時年四十八。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died, at the age of forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died, at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 高祖、文明太后親臨哀慟，賜溫明祕器，宕昌公王遇監護喪事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao and the Civilizing Empress Dowager personally came to mourn him in grief, bestowed a Wenming secret coffin, and Wang Yu, Prince of Dangchang, supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao and the Civilizing Empress Dowager personally came to mourn him in grief, bestowed a Wenming secret coffin, and Wang Yu, Prince of Dangchang, supervised the funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈衞大將軍、太宰、并州牧，諡曰宣王。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles Grand General of the Guard, Grand Marshal, and Governor of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title Prince Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles Grand General of the Guard, Grand Marshal, and Governor of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title Prince Xuan.

sentences.zh: 內侍長董醜奴營墳墓，將葬於城東，高祖登城樓以望之。

translations.literal: The chief eunuch Dong Chounu arranged the tomb, and when it was to be buried east of the city, Emperor Gao climbed the city tower to watch.
translations.idiomatic: The chief eunuch Dong Chounu arranged the tomb, and when it was to be buried east of the city, Emperor Gao climbed the city tower to watch.

sentences.zh: 京都文士為作哀詩及誄者百餘人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred literary men of the capital composed mourning poems and elegies for him.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred literary men of the capital composed mourning poems and elegies for him.

sentences.zh: 乃詔為叡立祀於都南二十里大道右，起廟以時祭薦，并立碑銘，置守祀五家。

translations.literal: Then an edict ordered that a shrine be established for Rui twenty li south of the capital, on the right side of the main road; a temple was built for seasonal sacrifices, along with a stele inscription, and five families were assigned to maintain the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Then an edict ordered that a shrine be established for Rui twenty li south of the capital, on the right side of the main road; a temple was built for seasonal sacrifices, along with a stele inscription, and five families were assigned to maintain the shrine.

sentences.zh: 又詔褒叡，圖其捍虎狀於諸殿，命高允為之讚。

translations.literal: Another edict praised Rui, had his tiger-defending pose painted in the various palaces, and ordered Gao Yun to compose a eulogy for it.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict praised Rui, had his tiger-defending pose painted in the various palaces, and ordered Gao Yun to compose a eulogy for it.

sentences.zh: 京都士女謟稱叡美，造新聲而絃歌之，名曰中山王樂。

translations.literal: The men and women of the capital flattered Rui's virtues, composed new airs, and sang them to string accompaniment, calling them Prince Zhongshan Music.
translations.idiomatic: The men and women of the capital flattered Rui's virtues, composed new airs, and sang them to string accompaniment, calling them Prince Zhongshan Music.

sentences.zh: 詔班樂府，合樂奏之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Music Bureau to record it and perform it as ensemble music.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Music Bureau to record it and perform it as ensemble music.

sentences.zh: 子襲，字元孫。

translations.literal: His son Xi, courtesy name Yuansun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi, courtesy name Yuansun.

sentences.zh: 年十四，以父任擢為中散，仍總中部。

translations.literal: At the age of fourteen, on account of his father's service, he was promoted to Zhongsan and given charge of the Middle Division.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of fourteen, on account of his father's service, he was promoted to Zhongsan and given charge of the Middle Division.

sentences.zh: 叡薨，高祖詔襲代領都曹，為尚書令，領吏部曹、中部，如其品職，依典承襲。

translations.literal: When Rui died, Emperor Gao ordered Xi to succeed him as head of the Dacao, made him Shangshu Ling, and put him in charge of the Civil Appointments Office and the Middle Division, letting him inherit the office in accordance with the established regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Rui died, Emperor Gao ordered Xi to succeed him as head of the Dacao, made him Shangshu Ling, and put him in charge of the Civil Appointments Office and the Middle Division, letting him inherit according to the established regulations.

sentences.zh: 文明太后令曰：「都曹尚書曹百僚之首，[1]民所具瞻。

translations.literal: The Civilizing Empress Dowager issued an edict saying: 'The Shangshu of the Dacao is the head of all officials and the object of all people's gaze.
translations.idiomatic: The Civilizing Empress Dowager issued an edict saying: 'The Shangshu of the Dacao is the head of all officials and the object of all people's gaze.

sentences.zh: 襲年少，智思未周，其都曹尚書令可權記，使閑習政事，後用不晚。

translations.literal: Xi is young, and his judgment and thought are not yet complete; the post of Shangshu Ling in the Dacao may be held provisionally, so that he may become familiar with government affairs, and he can be used later without it being too late.
translations.idiomatic: Xi is young, and his judgment and thought are not yet complete; the post of Shangshu Ling in the Dacao may be held provisionally, so that he may become familiar with government affairs, and he can be used later without delay.

sentences.zh: 」終太后世，寵念如初。

translations.literal: Throughout the empress dowager's reign, favor and regard remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the empress dowager's reign, favor and regard remained as before.

sentences.zh: 襲王爵，例降為公。

translations.literal: His princely title was, by custom, reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His princely title was, by custom, reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 太后崩後，襲仍在高祖左右，然禮遇稍薄，不復關與時事。

translations.literal: After the empress dowager died, Xi still remained at Emperor Gao's side, but the rites and favor shown to him grew somewhat thinner, and he was no longer involved in current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager died, Xi still remained at Emperor Gao's side, but the rites and favor shown to him grew somewhat thinner, and he was no longer involved in current affairs.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為鎮西將軍、秦州刺史，又轉并州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qinzhou, then transferred to Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qinzhou, then transferred to Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年，輿駕詣洛，路幸其治，供帳粗辦，境內清靜，高祖頗嘉之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when the imperial carriage went to Luoyang and passed through his jurisdiction on the way, the hospitality arrangements were only roughly prepared, but the prefecture was peaceful, so Emperor Gao praised him highly.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, when the imperial carriage went to Luoyang and passed through his jurisdiction on the way, the hospitality arrangements were only roughly prepared, but the prefecture was peaceful, so Emperor Gao praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 而民庶多為立銘，置于大路，虛相稱美，或曰襲所教也。

translations.literal: But many commoners had inscriptions set up for him and placed them on the main road, empty mutual praise, and some said Xi had taught them to do it.
translations.idiomatic: But many commoners had inscriptions set up for him and placed them on the main road, empty mutual praise, and some said Xi had taught them to do it.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而問之，對不以實，因是面被責讓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao heard of it and questioned him, he answered falsely, and for this he was rebuked in person.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao heard of it and questioned him, he answered falsely, and for this he was rebuked in person.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏免其官，詔唯降號二等。

translations.literal: The Shangshu bureau submitted a memorial asking that he be removed from office, and the edict merely demoted his title by two grades.
translations.idiomatic: The Shangshu bureau submitted a memorial asking that he be removed from office, and the edict merely demoted his title by two grades.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以事為中尉所糾，會赦免，語在常景傳。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was impeached by the censor over some matter; an amnesty happened to coincide, so he was pardoned. The story is in the biography of Chang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, he was impeached by the censor over some matter; an amnesty happened to coincide, so he was pardoned. The story is in the biography of Chang Jing.

sentences.zh: [2]景明二年卒，贈平南將軍、豫州刺史，諡曰質。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingming, he died and was posthumously granted the titles General Pacifying the South and Inspector of Yuzhou, with the posthumous title Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingming, he died and was posthumously granted the titles General Pacifying the South and Inspector of Yuzhou, with the posthumous title Zhi.

sentences.zh: 子忻，襲爵，為太尉、汝南王悅記室參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xin inherited the title and served as a records officer under the Grand Commandant and Prince of Runan Yue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin inherited the title and served as a records officer under the Grand Commandant and Prince of Runan Yue.

sentences.zh: 建義初，河陰遇害，贈散騎常侍、安北將軍、肆州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: At the start of the Jianyi era, he was killed at Heyin, and was posthumously granted the titles Palace Attendant, General Pacifying the North, and Inspector of Sizhou, with the posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era, he was killed at Heyin, and was posthumously granted the titles Palace Attendant, General Pacifying the North, and Inspector of Sizhou, with the posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 子子暄，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Zixuan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zixuan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定末，齊州驃騎府功曹參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wuding era, he served as Merit Officer-Captain in the Cavalry General's office of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era, he served as Merit Officer-Captain in the Cavalry General's office of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced as usual.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced as usual.

sentences.zh: 忻弟誕，字永安。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brother Dan, courtesy name Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's younger brother Dan, courtesy name Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍、正平太守。

translations.literal: He served as General of Dragon-Pulse and Prefect of Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General of Dragon-Pulse and Prefect of Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 亦於河陰遇害，贈撫軍將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: He too was killed at Heyin and was posthumously granted the titles General Pacifying the Army and Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He too was killed at Heyin and was posthumously granted the titles General Pacifying the Army and Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子希雲，舉秀才，早亡。

translations.literal: His son Xiyun was recommended as a xiaolian and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiyun was recommended as a xiaolian and died young.

sentences.zh: 誕弟殖，字永興。

translations.literal: Dan's younger brother Zhi, courtesy name Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's younger brother Zhi, courtesy name Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 司空城局參軍。

translations.literal: He served as a junior officer in the city bureau of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a junior officer in the city bureau of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子祖幹，司徒行參軍，并州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Zugan served as acting cadet officer in the Ministry of Personnel and as Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zugan served as acting cadet officer in the Ministry of Personnel and as Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 殖弟永業，司空參軍事。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Yongye served as a cadet officer under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Yongye served as a cadet officer under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 襲弟椿，字元壽。

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother Chun, courtesy name Yuanshou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Chun, courtesy name Yuanshou.

sentences.zh: 少以父任拜祕書中散，尋以父憂去職。

translations.literal: At a young age, on account of his father's service, he was appointed Secretary Bureau Zhongsan; soon after, he resigned because of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: At a young age, on account of his father's service, he was appointed Secretary Bureau Zhongsan; soon after, he resigned on the death of his father.

sentences.zh: 後除羽林監、謁者僕射，母喪解任。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Supervisor of the Royal Guards and deputy director of the gate attendants, but resigned when his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Supervisor of the Royal Guards and deputy director of the gate attendants, but laid down office when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 正始初，拜中散，出為太原太守，加鎮遠將軍，坐事免。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengshi, he was appointed Zhongsan, sent out as Prefect of Taiyuan, and added as General of Pacifying Distance, but was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhengshi, he was appointed Zhongsan, sent out as Prefect of Taiyuan, and given the added title of General of Pacifying Distance, but was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 椿僮僕千餘，園宅華廣，聲妓自適，無乏於時。

translations.literal: Chun had more than a thousand servants; his gardens and house were splendid and spacious, and musicians and singing girls amused him, so that nothing was lacking in those days.
translations.idiomatic: Chun had more than a thousand servants; his gardens and residence were splendid and spacious, and music girls and singing girls kept him amused, so that he lacked for nothing in those days.

sentences.zh: 或有勸椿仕者，椿笑而不答。

translations.literal: When some people urged Chun to take office, Chun only smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When some people urged Chun to take office, Chun only smiled and gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 雅有巧思，凡所營製，可為後法。

translations.literal: He had a refined gift for ingenuity, and everything he designed or built could serve as a model for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: He had a refined gift for ingenuity, and everything he designed or built could serve as a model for later generations.

sentences.zh: 由是正光中，元叉將營明堂、辟雍，欲徵椿為將作大匠，椿聞而以疾固辭。

translations.literal: Therefore, in Zhengguang, when Yuan Cha planned to build the Mingtang and Biyong and wanted to summon Chun as Grand Director of Construction, Chun heard of it and firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, in Zhengguang, when Yuan Cha planned to build the Mingtang and Biyong and wanted to summon Chun as Grand Director of Construction, Chun heard of it and firmly declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，尒朱榮既據并肆，以汾州胡逆，表加椿征虜將軍、都督，慰勞汾胡。

translations.literal: In Xiaochang, after Erzhu Rong had seized Bing and Si and because the Hu of Fenzhou were in rebellion, he memorialized to add Chun as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and commander, to go and console the Fenzhou Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang, after Erzhu Rong had seized Bing and Si and because the Hu of Fenzhou were in rebellion, he memorialized to add Chun as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and commander, to go and console the Fenzhou Hu.

sentences.zh: 汾胡與椿比州，服其聲望，所在降下。

translations.literal: The Fenzhou Hu were neighboring Chun's prefecture, and, impressed by his reputation, surrendered wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: The Fenzhou Hu lived in the same region as Chun, and, impressed by his reputation, surrendered wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 事寧，授右將軍、太原太守。

translations.literal: When affairs settled, he was appointed Right General and Prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs settled, he was appointed Right General and Prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 以預立莊帝之勞，封遼陽縣開國子，食邑三百戶，尋轉封真定縣開國侯，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: Because of his service in helping establish Emperor Zhuang, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Liyang County and granted 300 households; soon after, he was transferred and enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhengding County and granted 700 households.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his service in helping establish Emperor Zhuang, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Liyang County and granted 300 households; soon after, he was transferred and enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhengding County and granted 700 households.

sentences.zh: 除持節、本將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Holder of the Imperial Baton, with his former general rank, and Inspector of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Holder of the Imperial Baton, with his former general rank, and Inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 尋轉使持節、散騎常侍、殷州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after, he was transferred to be Imperial Envoy with baton, Palace Attendant, and Inspector of Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he was transferred to be Imperial Envoy with baton, Palace Attendant, and Inspector of Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 元曄立，除都官尚書，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was established, he was appointed Minister of the Court of Justice, but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was established, he was appointed Minister of the Court of Justice, but firmly declined and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，行冀州事。

translations.literal: In Yongxi, he was acting in charge of affairs in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi, he was acting in charge of affairs in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋除使持節、散騎常侍、車騎將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Imperial Envoy with baton, Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Imperial Envoy with baton, Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時有風雹之變，詔書廣訪讜言，椿乃上疏曰：「伏奉詔書，以風雹厲威，上動天睠，訪讜辭於百辟，詔輿誦於四海。

translations.literal: At a time when wind and hail disasters had occurred, an edict widely sought frank counsel, and Chun memorialized: 'I humbly receive the edict, which treats wind and hail as displays of stern power, moving the Heavenly gaze above and seeking candid words from the hundred officials while broadcasting the command throughout the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: At a time when wind and hail had caused calamity, an edict widely sought frank counsel, and Chun memorialized: 'I humbly receive the edict, which treats wind and hail as a show of stern power, moving Heaven's regard above and seeking candid words from the hundred officials while broadcasting the command throughout the four seas.

sentences.zh: 宸衷懇切，備在絲綸，祗承兢感，心焉靡厝。

translations.literal: The sovereign's concern is earnest and complete in the written decree; I receive it with reverence and trembling, and my heart has nowhere to put itself.
translations.idiomatic: Your sacred intention is earnest and complete in the imperial edict; I receive it with reverence and trembling, and my heart has nowhere to rest.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下啟籙應期，馭育萬物，承綴旒之艱運，纂纖絲之危緒，忘餐日昃，求衣未明，俾上帝下臨，愍茲荼蓼，永濟溝壑。

translations.literal: I humbly think Your Majesty has opened the tally and answered the age, guiding and nurturing all things, inheriting the hard fortunes of a drooping banner and continuing a thread of peril as thin as silk, forgetting meals at midday and seeking clothing before dawn, so that the Supreme Deity may descend, pity this bitter hardship, and help us forever across the ravines.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly think Your Majesty has opened the register and answered the age, guiding and nurturing all things, inheriting the hard fortunes of a drooping banner and continuing a thread of peril as thin as silk, forgetting meals at midday and seeking clothing before dawn, so that the Supreme Deity may descend, pity this bitter hardship, and forever help us across the ravines.

sentences.zh: 而滄浪降戾，作害中秋。

translations.literal: Yet the blue vault sent down its penalty and caused harm in mid-autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven sent down its penalty and wrought harm in mid-autumn.

sentences.zh: 上帝照臨，義不虛變。

translations.literal: The Supreme Deity looks down in illumination, so such a change cannot be without reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Deity looks down in illumination, so such a change cannot be without cause.

sentences.zh: 竊惟風為號令，皇天所以示威；

translations.literal: I privately think wind is the voice of commands, the means by which Heaven shows its power;
translations.idiomatic: I privately think wind is the voice of commands, the means by which Heaven shows its power.

sentences.zh: 雹者氣激，陰陽有所交諍。

translations.literal: Hail arises when qi surges, and yin and yang have some contention with one another.
translations.idiomatic: Hail arises when qi surges, and yin and yang contend with one another.

sentences.zh: 殆行令殊節，舒急失中之所致也。

translations.literal: It is probably caused by issuing orders at the wrong season and by losing the mean between slackness and haste.
translations.idiomatic: It is probably caused by issuing orders out of season and by losing the proper balance between slackness and haste.

sentences.zh: 昔澍雨千里，實緣教祀之誠；

translations.literal: In former times, when timely rain spread for a thousand li, it truly depended on sincerity in instruction and sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when timely rain spread for a thousand li, it truly depended on sincerity in teaching and sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 炎精三舍，寧非善言之力。

translations.literal: When the fiery essence moved three lodges, could that not have been the power of good words?
translations.idiomatic: When the fiery essence moved three lodges, could that not have been the power of good words?

sentences.zh: 譴不空發，徵豈謬應，誰謂蓋高，實符人事。

translations.literal: A reproach is not sent out in vain, and a sign does not answer by mistake; who says the canopy above is high? It in fact accords with human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A reproach is not sent out in vain, and a sign does not answer by mistake; who says Heaven is remote? It in fact accords with human affairs.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下留心曲覽，垂神遠察，禮賢登士，博舉審官，擢申滯怨，振窮省役。

translations.literal: I humbly beg Your Majesty to give this close attention and a careful reading, to extend your spirit to distant scrutiny, honor the worthy and elevate the able, make broad and careful appointments, promote the long-suppressed and aggrieved, and relieve the poor while reducing labor service.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to give this close attention and a careful reading, to extend your spirit to distant scrutiny, honor the worthy and elevate the able, make broad and careful appointments, promote the long-suppressed and aggrieved, and relieve the poor while reducing labor service.

sentences.zh: 使夫滋水沒川之彥，[3]畢居朝右；

translations.literal: So that men of talent like the gentleman of the flooded Zi River [3] may all dwell to the right of the court;
translations.idiomatic: So that men of talent like the gentleman of the flooded Zi River [3] may all dwell to the right of the court;

sentences.zh: 儀表丹青之位，未或虛加。

translations.literal: And that the offices of exemplar and portrait may never be granted in vain.
translations.idiomatic: And that the offices of exemplar and portrait may never be granted in vain.

sentences.zh: 圜土絕五毒之民，揆日息千門之費。

translations.literal: Let the prison grounds be rid of the people of the five poisons, and by careful reckoning let the expenses of a thousand gates cease.
translations.idiomatic: Let the prison grounds be rid of the people of the five poisons, and by careful reckoning let the expenses of a thousand gates cease.

sentences.zh: 巖巖廊署，無不遇之士；

translations.literal: In the lofty halls and offices, there should be no worthy man left unencountered;
translations.idiomatic: In the lofty halls and offices, there should be no worthy man left unencountered;

sentences.zh: 忪忪惸獨，荷酒帛之恩。

translations.literal: And the anxious, lonely, and helpless should bear the favor of wine and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: And the anxious, lonely, and helpless should bear the favor of wine and cloth.

sentences.zh: 則物見昭蘇，人知休泰，徐奏薰風之曲，無論鴻雁之歌，豈不天人幸甚，鬼神咸抃？」

translations.literal: Then creatures will seem renewed and people will know peace; if one slowly plays the music of the fragrant wind, not to mention the song of the wild geese, would this not bring great fortune to heaven and humanity alike, with ghosts and spirits all clapping?
translations.idiomatic: Then creatures will seem renewed and people will know peace; if one slowly plays the music of the fragrant wind, not to mention the song of the wild geese, would this not bring great fortune to heaven and humanity alike, with ghosts and spirits all clapping?

sentences.zh: 椿性嚴察，下不容姦，所在吏民，畏之重足。

translations.literal: Chun's nature was stern and discerning; he tolerated no corruption below him, and officials and commoners wherever he served feared him so much that they could barely move.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's nature was stern and discerning; he tolerated no corruption below him, and officials and commoners wherever he served feared him so much that they could barely move.

sentences.zh: 天平末，更滿還鄉。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianping, when his term was finished, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianping, when his term was finished, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 初椿於宅構起廳事，極為高壯。

translations.literal: At first Chun built a hall in his residence, extremely tall and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: At first Chun built a hall in his residence, extremely tall and imposing.

sentences.zh: 時人忽云：「此乃太原王宅，豈是王太原宅。

translations.literal: At the time people suddenly said, 'This is the mansion of Wang of Taiyuan; how could it be the Taiyuan mansion of Wang?
translations.idiomatic: At the time people suddenly said, 'This is the mansion of Wang of Taiyuan; how could it be the Taiyuan mansion of Wang?

sentences.zh: 」椿往為本郡，世皆呼為王太原。

translations.literal: When Chun had served as prefect there, everyone in the world called him Wang Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Chun had served as prefect there, everyone in the world called him Wang Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，尒朱榮居椿之宅，榮封太原王焉。

translations.literal: Not long after, Erzhu Rong occupied Chun's house, and Rong was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Erzhu Rong occupied Chun's house, and Rong was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 至於齊獻武王之居晉陽，霸朝所在，人士輻湊。

translations.literal: By the time Prince Xianwu of Qi dwelt in Jinyang, where the hegemonic court was located, men of talent flocked there.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Prince Xianwu of Qi dwelt in Jinyang, where the hegemonic court was located, men of talent flocked there.

sentences.zh: 椿禮敬親知，多所拯接。

translations.literal: Chun was courteous and respectful toward relatives and acquaintances, and helped many of them.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was courteous and respectful toward relatives and acquaintances, and helped many of them.

sentences.zh: 後以老病，遂辭疾客居趙郡之西鯉魚祠山。

translations.literal: Later, because of age and illness, he resigned on grounds of illness and lived as a guest on West Carp Shrine Mountain in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because of age and illness, he resigned on grounds of illness and lived as a guest on West Carp Shrine Mountain in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 興和二年春卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: He died in the spring of the second year of Xinghe, at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the spring of the second year of Xinghe, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、都督冀瀛二州軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、太尉公、冀州刺史，諡曰文恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles Imperial Envoy with Baton, Commander of the Military Affairs of Jizhou and Yingzhou, Grand General of the Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Shangshu, Grand Commandant, and Inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles Imperial Envoy with Baton, Commander of the Military Affairs of Jizhou and Yingzhou, Grand General of the Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Shangshu, Grand Commandant, and Inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Wengong.

sentences.zh: 及葬，齊獻武王親自弔送。

translations.literal: At the burial, Prince Xianwu of Qi personally came to mourn and escort the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial, Prince Xianwu of Qi personally came to mourn and escort the coffin.

sentences.zh: 椿妻鉅鹿魏悅之次女，明達有遠操，多識往行前言。

translations.literal: Chun's wife was the second daughter of Wei Yuezhi of Julu; she was intelligent, clear-sighted, and possessed of far-reaching conduct, and knew much of earlier deeds and sayings.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's wife was the second daughter of Wei Yuezhi of Julu; she was intelligent, clear-sighted, and possessed of far-reaching conduct, and knew much of earlier deeds and sayings.

sentences.zh: 隨夫在華州，兄子建在洛遇患，聞而星夜馳赴，膚容虧損，親類歎尚之。

translations.literal: While following her husband in Huazhou, when her brother's son Jian fell ill in Luoyang, she heard of it and rode there day and night, her complexion and features wasting away, and her relatives praised her for it.
translations.idiomatic: While following her husband in Huazhou, when her brother's son Jian fell ill in Luoyang, she heard of it and rode there day and night, her complexion and features wasting away, and her relatives praised her for it.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮妻北鄉郡長公主深所禮敬。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong's wife, the Great Princess of Beixiang Commandery, held her in deep respect.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong's wife, the Great Princess of Beixiang Commandery, held her in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 永安中，詔以為南和縣君。

translations.literal: In Yong'an, an edict made her Lady of Nanhe County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an, an edict made her Lady of Nanhe County.

sentences.zh: 內足於財，不以華飾為意。

translations.literal: She had enough wealth within her household and took no interest in ornament and finery.
translations.idiomatic: She had enough wealth within her household and took no interest in ornament and finery.

sentences.zh: 撫兄子收情同己子，存拯親類，所在周洽。

translations.literal: She cared for her brother's son with the same affection as for her own child, and supported her relatives, meeting their needs wherever they were.
translations.idiomatic: She cared for her brother's son with the same affection as for her own child, and supported her relatives, meeting their needs wherever they were.

sentences.zh: 椿名位終始，魏有力焉。

translations.literal: Throughout Chun's rise and standing, Wei had much to do with it.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Chun's rise and standing, Wei had much to do with it.

sentences.zh: 元象中卒，贈鉅鹿郡君。

translations.literal: She died in the Yuanxiang period and was posthumously granted the title Lady of Julu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the Yuanxiang period and was posthumously granted the title Lady of Julu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 椿無子，以兄孫叔明為後。

translations.literal: Chun had no son, so he took his brother's grandson Shuming as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Chun had no son, so he took his brother's grandson Shuming as heir.

sentences.zh: 叔明，太尉參軍事、儀同開府祭酒。

translations.literal: Shuming served as a staff officer to the Grand Commandant and as libationer of the Yitong open house.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming served as a staff officer to the Grand Commandant and as libationer of the Yitong open house.

sentences.zh: 死於晉陽，無子，以弟子暄子為後。

translations.literal: He died in Jinyang without a son, so he took his brother Zixuan's son as heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jinyang without a son, so he took his brother Zixuan's son as heir.

sentences.zh: 叡弟諶，字厚誠。

translations.literal: Rui's younger brother Shen, courtesy name Houcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's younger brother Shen bore the courtesy name Houcheng.

sentences.zh: 為給事中、安南將軍、祠部尚書，賜爵上黨公。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Gentleman, General Pacifying the South, and Minister of Sacrifices, and was granted the title Duke of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant Gentleman, General Pacifying the South, and Minister of Sacrifices, and was granted the title Duke of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍，領太史事。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Palace Attendant and put in charge of the Grand Astrologer Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Palace Attendant and put in charge of the Grand Astrologer Bureau.

sentences.zh: 例降為侯。

translations.literal: By custom his rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: By custom his rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 遷太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of the Taichang.

sentences.zh: 出為持節、安東將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Holder of the Imperial Baton, General Pacifying the East, and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Holder of the Imperial Baton, General Pacifying the East, and Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，除光祿大夫，卒於官。

translations.literal: On his return, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Hospitality, and died while in office.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Hospitality, and died while in office.

sentences.zh: 贈帛五十匹。

translations.literal: He was given fifty bolts of silk in posthumous tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He was given fifty bolts of silk in posthumous tribute.

sentences.zh: 子翔，字元鳳。

translations.literal: His son Xiang, courtesy name Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang bore the courtesy name Yuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 少以聰敏循良，詔充內侍。

translations.literal: He was young, clever, and upright, and by edict was appointed to the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: He was young, clever, and upright, and by edict was appointed to the inner court.

sentences.zh: 自太和初，與李沖等奏決庶事，迄于十六年，賞賜前後累千萬。

translations.literal: From the start of Taihe, together with Li Chong and others he helped decide the many affairs of state; by the sixteenth year, the rewards and gifts bestowed on him had accumulated to the millions.
translations.idiomatic: From the start of Taihe, together with Li Chong and others he helped decide the many affairs of state; by the sixteenth year, the rewards and gifts bestowed on him had accumulated to the millions.

sentences.zh: 是時政事多決於文明太后，后好細察，而翔恭謹慎密，甚被知任。

translations.literal: At that time most state affairs were decided by the Civilizing Empress Dowager. She favored close scrutiny, and Xiang was respectful, careful, and discreet, so he was greatly trusted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time most state affairs were decided by the Civilizing Empress Dowager. She favored close scrutiny, and Xiang was respectful, careful, and discreet, so he was greatly trusted and employed.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，兼給事黃門侍郎、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When the court moved to Luoyang, he concurrently served as Yellow Gate Attendant Gentleman and Left Assistant Director of the Shangshu.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Luoyang, he concurrently served as Yellow Gate Attendant Gentleman and Left Assistant Director of the Shangshu.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，遷輔國將軍、太府少卿。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and was promoted to General Assisting the State and Vice Minister of the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and was promoted to General Assisting the State and Vice Minister of the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 出為濟州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈大將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: He died, and was posthumously granted the titles Great General and Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and was posthumously granted the titles Great General and Inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 子超，襲。

translations.literal: His son Chao inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 超，字和善。

translations.literal: Chao, courtesy name Heshan.
translations.idiomatic: Chao bore the courtesy name Heshan.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請、并州治中。

translations.literal: He served as an attendant to the court audience and as Chancellor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an attendant to the court audience and as Chancellor of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 超愛好人物，輕財重義。

translations.literal: Chao loved people and held righteousness above wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Chao valued people and held righteousness above wealth.

sentences.zh: 性豪華，能自奉養，每食必窮水陸之味。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant and could support himself well; every meal had to include the finest land and sea delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant and could support himself well; every meal had to include the finest land and sea delicacies.

sentences.zh: 年三十四卒。

translations.literal: He died at the age of thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 子景覽，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jinglan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jinglan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定中，衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During Wuding, he served as Guard General and Right Grand Master of Splendid Hospitality.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuding, he served as Guard General and Right Grand Master of Splendid Hospitality.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced as usual.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced as usual.

sentences.zh: 景覽弟景招，開府集曹參軍。

translations.literal: Jinglan's younger brother Jingzhao served as a cadet officer in the Open House's Administrative Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglan's younger brother Jingzhao served as a cadet officer in the Open House's Administrative Bureau.

sentences.zh: 超弟穆，字思泰。

translations.literal: Chao's younger brother Mu, courtesy name Sitai.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's younger brother Mu bore the courtesy name Sitai.

sentences.zh: 元象中，上黨太守。

translations.literal: In Yuanxiang, he was Prefect of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxiang, he was Prefect of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 穆弟綽，字思和，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Mu's younger brother Chuo, courtesy name Sihe, was an attendant gentleman without regular office.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's younger brother Chuo, courtesy name Sihe, was an attendant gentleman without regular office.

sentences.zh: 上黨王天穆以為北道行臺郎中。

translations.literal: Prince Tianmu of Shangdang appointed him Langzhong of the Northern Route Executive Office.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tianmu of Shangdang appointed him Langzhong of the Northern Route Executive Office.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮代天穆為大行臺，仍為吏部郎。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong replaced Tianmu as Grand Executive Commissioner, Chuo remained as Personnel Bureau officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong replaced Tianmu as Grand Executive Commissioner, Chuo remained as a Personnel Bureau officer.

sentences.zh: 以預奉莊帝之勳，封猗氏縣開國侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Because of his merit in assisting the enthronement of Emperor Zhuang, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yishi County with 500 households.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his merit in assisting the enthronement of Emperor Zhuang, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yishi County with 500 households.

sentences.zh: 永安末，除征西將軍、豳州刺史，不之任。

translations.literal: At the end of Yong'an, he was appointed General of the Western Campaign and Inspector of Binzhou, but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yong'an, he was appointed General of the Western Campaign and Inspector of Binzhou, but did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 元曄立，轉除驃騎大將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was established, he was transferred to be Great General of the Cavalry and Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was established, he was transferred to be Great General of the Cavalry and Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 興和中卒。

translations.literal: He died during Xinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He died during Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 綽弟爽，司徒中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Chuo's younger brother Shuang served as cadet officer in the army bureau of the Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo's younger brother Shuang served as cadet officer in the army bureau of the Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 諶弟魏誠，為東宮學生，拜給事中，賜爵中都侯，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Shen's younger brother Weicheng was a student of the Eastern Palace; he was appointed Attendant Gentleman, granted the title Marquis of Zhongdu, and added as General of Dragon-Pulse.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's younger brother Weicheng was a student of the Eastern Palace; he was appointed Attendant Gentleman, granted the title Marquis of Zhongdu, and added as General of Dragon-Pulse.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安南將軍、冀州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted the titles General Pacifying the South and Inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the titles General Pacifying the South and Inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 子靜，字元安，少有公幹。

translations.literal: His son Jing, courtesy name Yuan'an, was capable from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing, courtesy name Yuan'an, was capable from youth.

sentences.zh: 拜中散，襲爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Zhongsan, inherited the title, and by custom was reduced to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Zhongsan, inherited the title, and by custom was reduced to viscount.

sentences.zh: 除員外郎、羽林監、兼尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Outer Gentleman, Supervisor of the Royal Guards, and concurrently Gentleman of the Shangshu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Outer Gentleman, Supervisor of the Royal Guards, and concurrently Gentleman of the Shangshu.

sentences.zh: 以明法除廷尉評。

translations.literal: Because he was versed in the law, he was appointed Judicial Review Officer in the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was versed in the law, he was appointed Judicial Review Officer in the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 轉游擊將軍，加冠軍將軍、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Guerrilla Cavalry, with the added titles of Champion General and Inspector of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of Guerrilla Cavalry, with the added titles of Champion General and Inspector of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王謐虐害，城民怨叛，詔靜以驛慰喻，咸即降下。

translations.literal: Because Prince Mi of Zhaojun was cruel and harmful, the townspeople grew resentful and rebelled; an edict ordered Jing to use the relay stations to comfort and persuade them, and they all immediately submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Because Prince Mi of Zhaojun was cruel and harmful, the townspeople grew resentful and rebelled; an edict ordered Jing to use the relay stations to comfort and persuade them, and they all immediately submitted.

sentences.zh: 以奉使稱旨，賜帛五百匹。

translations.literal: Because he fulfilled his mission to the emperor's satisfaction, he was given 500 bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Because he fulfilled his mission to the emperor's satisfaction, he was given 500 bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 除趙郡太守，以母老固辭不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Zhaojun, but firmly declined because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Prefect of Zhaojun, but firmly declined because his mother was old.

sentences.zh: 又授征虜將軍、廷尉少卿，有當官之稱。

translations.literal: He was also appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Junior Minister of the Court of Justice, and had a reputation for being fit for office.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Junior Minister of the Court of Justice, and had a reputation for being fit for office.

sentences.zh: 坐公事左遷中散大夫，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Because of an official matter, he was demoted to Middle Gentleman, and left office on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Because of an official matter, he was demoted to Middle Gentleman, and left office on account of his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，詔兼廷尉卿，尋行定州事，並固辭不起。

translations.literal: At the start of Xiaochang, he was ordered to concurrently serve as Minister of Justice, and soon to act in Dingzhou affairs; he firmly declined both and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiaochang, he was ordered to concurrently serve as Minister of Justice, and soon to act in Dingzhou affairs; he firmly declined both and did not take office.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，除長兼廷尉卿，尋行定州事。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year, he was appointed Long-Concurrent Minister of Justice, and soon acted in Dingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year, he was appointed Long-Concurrent Minister of Justice, and soon acted in Dingzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 至冬病卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In winter he died of illness, at the age of fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he died of illness, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈撫軍將軍、并州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles General Pacifying the Army and Inspector of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles General Pacifying the Army and Inspector of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 無子，以從子伯豫為後。

translations.literal: Having no son, he took his collateral son Boyu as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, he took his collateral son Boyu as heir.

sentences.zh: 伯豫，襲爵。

translations.literal: Boyu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定中，冀州開府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: During Wuding, he served as Recording Officer of the Open House in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuding, he served as Recording Officer of the Open House in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced as usual.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced as usual.

sentences.zh: 魏誠弟亮，字平誠。

translations.literal: Liang, younger brother of Weicheng, courtesy name Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, younger brother of Weicheng, bore the courtesy name Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 承明初，擢為中散。

translations.literal: At the start of Chengming, he was promoted to Zhongsan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Chengming, he was promoted to Zhongsan.

sentences.zh: 告沙門法秀反，遷冠軍將軍，賜爵永寧侯，加給事中。

translations.literal: After reporting the rebellion of the monk Faxiu, he was promoted to Champion General, granted the title Marquis of Yongning, and added as Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: After reporting the rebellion of the monk Faxiu, he was promoted to Champion General, granted the title Marquis of Yongning, and added as Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 出為安西將軍、泰州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General Pacifying the West and Inspector of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Pacifying the West and Inspector of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 後轉陝州刺史，坐事免。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Inspector of Shanzhou, but was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Inspector of Shanzhou, but was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 亮子洪壽，早卒。

translations.literal: Liang's son Hongshou died young.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's son Hongshou died young.

sentences.zh: 子元景，正光中許復先爵，降為伯。

translations.literal: His son Yuanjing was allowed in Zhengguang to recover the former title, but it was reduced to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanjing was allowed in Zhengguang to recover the former title, but it was reduced to viscount.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died without a son.
translations.idiomatic: He died without a son.

sentences.zh: 洪壽弟嶷，字安壽。

translations.literal: Hongshou's younger brother Ni, courtesy name Anshou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongshou's younger brother Ni bore the courtesy name Anshou.

sentences.zh: 除奉朝請，稍遷中散大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed to attend the court audience and was gradually promoted to Middle Gentleman Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to attend the court audience and was gradually promoted to Middle Gentleman Grandee.

sentences.zh: 以疾歸鄉里，遂移居上黨。

translations.literal: Because of illness he returned to his native place and then moved to Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he returned to his native place and then moved to Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 年七十一卒。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 子夷，字景預。

translations.literal: His son Yi, courtesy name Jingyu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi bore the courtesy name Jingyu.

sentences.zh: 有文才，少工詩詠，知名於世。

translations.literal: He had literary talent and, from youth, was skilled in poetry, becoming well known in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He had literary talent and, from youth, was skilled in poetry, becoming well known in the world.

sentences.zh: 未官而卒。

translations.literal: He died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: He died before taking office.

sentences.zh: 叡叔隆保，冠軍將軍、姑臧侯。

translations.literal: Rui's uncle Longbao was Champion General and Marquis of Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's uncle Longbao was Champion General and Marquis of Guzang.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈安東將軍、并州刺史，鉅鹿公，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted the titles General Pacifying the East, Inspector of Bingzhou, and Duke of Julu, with the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the titles General Pacifying the East, Inspector of Bingzhou, and Duke of Julu, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 王仲興，趙郡南欒人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongxing was a man of Nanluan in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongxing was a man of Nanluan in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: [4]父天德，起自細微，至殿中尚書。

translations.literal: His father Tiande rose from humble beginnings to become Minister of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tiande rose from humble beginnings to become Minister of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仲興幼而端謹，以父任早給事左右。

translations.literal: Zhongxing was upright and cautious from youth, and because of his father's service was early appointed to serve at court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing was upright and cautious from youth, and because of his father's service was early appointed to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 太和中，殿內侍御中散、武騎侍郎、給事中。

translations.literal: During Taihe he served as Palace Attendant Zhongsan, Gentleman of the Cavalry, and Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he served as Palace Attendant Zhongsan, Gentleman of the Cavalry, and Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 出入禁內十餘年，轉冗從僕射，猶參密近，為齋帥。

translations.literal: He spent more than ten years in and out of the inner palace, was transferred to deputy director of the miscellaneous attendants, and still took part in the confidential inner circle as a hall chief.
translations.idiomatic: He spent more than ten years in and out of the inner palace, was transferred to deputy director of the miscellaneous attendants, and still took part in the confidential inner circle as a hall chief.

sentences.zh: [5]從駕征新野有功，除折衝將軍、屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: For merit in accompanying the emperor on the campaign against Xinye, he was appointed General of Breakthrough and Cavalry Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in accompanying the emperor on the campaign against Xinye, he was appointed General of Breakthrough and Cavalry Colonel.

sentences.zh: 又命率千餘騎破賊於鄧城。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to lead more than a thousand cavalry to defeat the rebels at Dengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to lead more than a thousand cavalry to defeat the rebels at Dengcheng.

sentences.zh: 除振威將軍、越騎校尉，賜帛千匹。

translations.literal: Appointed as General Who Rouses Valor and Colonel of the Yue Cavalry, and granted a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Rouses Valor and Colonel of the Yue Cavalry, and awarded a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 尚書後以仲興開國公，賞報過優。

translations.literal: Later the Secretariat made Zhongxing a founding duke, and the rewards and repayment were excessive and overly generous.
translations.idiomatic: Later, the Secretariat made Zhongxing a founding duke, and his rewards were excessive and far too generous.

sentences.zh: 北海王詳嘗面啟奏請降減，事久不決。

translations.literal: The Prince of Beihai, Xiang, once personally memorialized the throne and asked that it be reduced, but the matter dragged on without decision.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Beihai, Xiang, once personally petitioned for a reduction, but the matter remained undecided for a long time.

sentences.zh: 可久在徐州，恃仲興寵勢，輕侮司馬、梁郡太守李長壽，遂至忿諍。

translations.literal: Kejiu, while in Xuzhou, relied on Zhongxing's favor and influence, and slighted and insulted the Sima and Commandant of Liang Commandery, Li Changshou, until the two came to blows in anger.
translations.idiomatic: While in Xuzhou, Kejiu relied on Zhongxing's favor and power and treated Li Changshou, the Sima and Commandant of Liang Commandery, with contempt, until the quarrel turned bitter.

sentences.zh: 彭城諸沙門共相和解，未幾，復有所競。

translations.literal: The monks of Pengcheng all tried to mediate and reconcile them, but before long there was again some dispute.
translations.idiomatic: The monks of Pengcheng mediated and settled matters between them, but before long another dispute arose.

sentences.zh: 可久乃令僮僕邀毆長壽，遂折其脅。

translations.literal: Kejiu then ordered his servants to ambush and beat Changshou, breaking one of his ribs.
translations.idiomatic: Kejiu then sent his servants to ambush and beat Changshou, breaking his ribs.

sentences.zh: 州以表聞。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported the matter by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture submitted a memorial reporting the matter.
