sentences.zh: 北海王詳因百僚朝集，厲色大言曰：「徐州名藩，先帝所重，朝廷云何簡用上佐，遂令致此紛紜，以徹荒外，豈不為國醜辱也！

translations.literal: The Prince of Beihai, Xiang, took advantage of a court gathering of the hundred officials, and said sternly and loudly: "Xuzhou is a renowned border fief, highly esteemed by the former emperor. How could the court so carelessly employ its deputy and thus bring about such turmoil, spreading it even to the remote frontier? Would this not bring shame and disgrace upon the state!
translations.idiomatic: At a court assembly of the hundred officials, the Prince of Beihai, Xiang, said sternly and at length: "Xuzhou is a famed frontier commandery, prized by the former emperor. How could the court appoint a deputy so carelessly and let matters sink into such disorder, spreading even to the remote borderlands? Is this not a disgrace to the state!

sentences.zh: 」眾亦莫有應者。

translations.literal: No one among the crowd answered him.
translations.idiomatic: No one in the crowd replied.

sentences.zh: 仲興是後漸疏，不得徑入左右。

translations.literal: After this, Zhongxing gradually became estranged and could no longer enter directly among the attendants.
translations.idiomatic: After this, Zhongxing was gradually kept at a distance and no longer had direct access to the emperor's attendants.

sentences.zh: 世宗乃下詔奪其封邑，出除平北將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong then issued an edict stripping him of his fief and sending him out to be appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong then issued an edict stripping him of his fief and sending him out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted the title General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: On his death, he was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 寇猛，上谷人也。

translations.literal: Kou Meng was a man of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Meng was a native of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 祖父平城。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 猛少以姿幹充虎賁，稍遷羽林中郎。

translations.literal: In youth Meng was selected for the Tiger Guards on account of his bearing and build, and was gradually promoted to Yu Lin Zhonglang.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, Meng was chosen for the Tiger Guards for his looks and physique, and was later promoted to Yu Lin Zhonglang.

sentences.zh: 從高祖征南陽，以擊賊不進免官。

translations.literal: He followed Gaozu in the campaign against Nanyang, but was dismissed from office for failing to press the attack against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gaozu on the campaign against Nanyang, but was dismissed for failing to press the attack on the bandits.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐位，復敍用，愛其膂力，置之左右，為千牛備身，歷轉遂至武衞將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was restored to employment. Admiring his strength, the emperor placed him among his attendants, made him a Thousand-Armor Attendant, and through successive transfers he ultimately rose to be General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was restored to office. Admiring his strength, the emperor kept him close at hand as a Thousand-Armor Attendant, and through successive transfers he eventually rose to General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 出入禁中，無所拘忌。

translations.literal: He came and went in the palace without any restraint or scruple.
translations.idiomatic: He came and went in the palace with no restraint whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 自以上谷寇氏，得補燕州大中正，而不能甄別士庶也。

translations.literal: Because he was of the Kou clan of Shanggu, he obtained appointment as Grand Arbiter of Yanzhou, but he was unable to distinguish between gentlemen and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was of the Kou clan of Shanggu, he was appointed Grand Arbiter of Yanzhou, but he could not distinguish the gentry from the common people.

sentences.zh: 家漸富侈，宅宇高華，妾隸充溢。

translations.literal: His household gradually became wealthy and extravagant, his residence tall and splendid, with concubines and slaves filling it to overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: His household grew increasingly rich and lavish, his home tall and splendid, with concubines and servants filling it to overflowing.

sentences.zh: 微榮弟姪，然不及茹皓、仲興也。

translations.literal: He brought some honor to his younger brothers and nephews, but not to the extent of Ru Hao and Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: He brought a measure of honor to his younger brothers and nephews, though not to the extent of Ru Hao and Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平北將軍、燕州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted the title General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his death, he was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 趙脩，字景業，趙郡房子人。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiu, courtesy name Jingye, was a man of Fangzi in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiu, courtesy name Jingye, was a native of Fangzi in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父惠安，後名謐，都曹史，積勞補陽武令。

translations.literal: His father was Hui'an, later named Mi, who served as Registrar of the Capital Offices and, after accumulating merit through long service, was appointed Magistrate of Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Hui'an, later renamed Mi, who served as a clerk in the Capital Offices and, after long service, was appointed Magistrate of Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 脩貴，追贈威烈將軍、本郡太守，及葬，復贈龍驤將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: When Xiu became eminent, his father was posthumously awarded the title General of Majestic Valor and Commandant of his native commandery; at the burial he was further posthumously granted the title General of Dragon Soar and Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu rose to prominence, his father was posthumously honored as General of Majestic Valor and Commandant of his home commandery; at the burial he was further granted the title General of Dragon Soar and Inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 脩本給事東宮，為白衣左右，頗有膂力。

translations.literal: Xiu had originally served in the Eastern Palace as an attendant in plain clothes and possessed considerable strength.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had originally served in the Eastern Palace as a plainclothes attendant and was quite strong.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，仍充禁侍，愛遇日隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Xiu continued as a palace attendant, and the emperor's favor toward him grew day by day.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Xiu continued as a palace attendant, and the emperor's favor toward him grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 然天性闇塞，不閑書疏，是故不參文墨。

translations.literal: But he was dull by nature and unskilled at written documents, so he took no part in literary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: But he was dull by nature and unskilled at written documents, so he took no part in literary affairs.

sentences.zh: 世宗親政，旬月之間，頻有轉授，歷員外通直散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、光祿卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took personal control of government, within the space of a month he repeatedly received new appointments, serving successively as Gentleman Attendant of the Regular Audience without Concurrent Office, General Who Guards the East, and Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took personal control of government, Xiu was repeatedly promoted within a month, serving successively as Gentleman Attendant of the Regular Audience without Concurrent Office, General Who Guards the East, and Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 每受除設宴，世宗親幸其宅，諸王公卿士百僚悉從，世宗親見其母。

translations.literal: Whenever he received an appointment, a banquet was held, and Emperor Shizong would personally visit his home, with all the princes, dukes, nobles, scholars, and officials following; Emperor Shizong also personally met his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xiu received a new appointment, a banquet was held, and Emperor Shizong would personally visit his home, with all the princes, dukes, ministers, and officials following along; the emperor also personally met Xiu's mother.

sentences.zh: 脩能劇飲，至於逼勸觴爵，雖北海王詳、廣陽王嘉等皆亦不免，必致困亂。

translations.literal: Xiu was able to drink heavily, to the point of forcing others to drink; even the Prince of Beihai, Xiang, the Prince of Guangyang, Jia, and others were all unable to avoid it, and were sure to become intoxicated and disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu could drink heavily and would even press others to drink; even the Prince of Beihai, Xiang, and the Prince of Guangyang, Jia, were not spared and would inevitably end up drunk and disordered.

sentences.zh: 每適郊廟，脩常驂陪。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went to the suburban sacrifices or ancestral temples, Xiu customarily rode as a companion in the side horse.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went to the suburban altars or ancestral temples, Xiu customarily rode alongside him.

sentences.zh: 出入華林，恒乘馬至于禁內。

translations.literal: When going in and out of Hualin, he always rode a horse all the way into the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: When going in and out of Hualin, he always rode his horse all the way into the forbidden precincts.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧誅，其家財貨多賜高肇及脩。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, was executed, much of his household property and wealth was bestowed upon Gao Zhao and Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, was executed, much of his family's property and wealth was given to Gao Zhao and Xiu.

sentences.zh: 脩之葬父也，百僚自王公以下無不弔祭，酒犢祭奠之具，填塞門街。

translations.literal: When Xiu buried his father, all the officials, from princes and dukes down, came without exception to offer condolences and sacrifice, and the wine, calves, and offerings filled the gate and street.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu buried his father, every official from princes and dukes downward came to offer condolences and sacrifice, and wine, calves, and burial offerings filled the gate and street.

sentences.zh: 於京師為制碑銘，石獸、石柱皆發民車牛，傳致本縣。

translations.literal: When a stele inscription was made for him in the capital, the stone animals and stone pillars were all transported to his home county using the carts and oxen of the people.
translations.idiomatic: When a stele inscription was made for him in the capital, the stone animals and stone pillars were all hauled to his home county using the carts and oxen of the people.

sentences.zh: 財用之費，悉自公家。

translations.literal: All expenses for materials and supplies came entirely from public funds.
translations.idiomatic: All expenses for materials and supplies were paid entirely from public funds.

sentences.zh: 凶吉車乘將百兩，道路供給，亦皆出官。

translations.literal: For the mourning and celebratory carriages, nearly a hundred vehicles were involved, and provisions along the road were likewise all supplied by the government.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly a hundred carriages were used for funerals and celebrations, and all provisions along the road were likewise supplied by the government.

sentences.zh: 時將馬射，世宗留脩過之。

translations.literal: At the time of the horse archery event, Emperor Shizong kept Xiu behind to wait on him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of the mounted archery event, Emperor Shizong kept Xiu behind to attend him.

sentences.zh: 帝如射宮，脩又驂乘，輅車旒竿觸東門而折。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to the archery palace, Xiu again rode as attendant in the carriage, and the banner pole on the imperial carriage struck the eastern gate and broke.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to the archery palace, Xiu again rode beside him, and the banner pole on the imperial carriage struck the eastern gate and snapped.

sentences.zh: 脩恐不逮葬日，驛赴窆期，左右求從及特遣者數十人。

translations.literal: Fearing he would not reach the burial date in time, Xiu rode post-haste to meet the interment deadline, with several dozen attendants, people he requested to accompany him, and specially dispatched men.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would not reach the burial day in time, Xiu rode hard by relay to the scheduled interment, with several dozen attendants, requested followers, and men specially sent with him.

sentences.zh: 脩道路嬉戲，殆無戚容，或與賓客姦掠婦女裸觀，從者噂𠴲喧譁，詬詈無節，莫不畏而惡之。

translations.literal: Along the road Xiu played and joked, showing scarcely any sign of grief; sometimes he and his guests sexually assaulted and plundered women for naked viewing. His followers chattered and shouted uproariously, cursing without restraint, so that all feared and loathed him.
translations.idiomatic: Along the road Xiu joked and cavorted, showing scarcely any grief. At times he and his guests assaulted women and stripped them for lewd display. His followers shouted and brawled without restraint, cursing freely, and everyone feared and despised him.

sentences.zh: 是年，又為脩廣增宅舍，多所并兼，洞門高堂，房廡周博，崇麗擬於諸王。

translations.literal: That year, they also greatly enlarged Xiu's houses, annexing many neighboring properties; with arched gates and lofty halls, the rooms and wings were broad and spacious, and their grandeur and splendor rivaled that of the princes.
translations.idiomatic: That year his residences were greatly expanded, with many neighboring properties annexed; the arched gates and lofty halls, the broad rooms and wings, and the magnificence of the whole rivaled that of the princes.

sentences.zh: 其四面隣居，賂入其地者侯天盛兄弟，越次出補長史、大郡。

translations.literal: His four-side neighbors, the Hou Tiancheng brothers, entered his land by bribery and were promoted beyond their rank to serve as chief clerks and in major commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His neighbors on all four sides, the Hou Tiancheng brothers, bribed their way into his land and were promoted beyond their station to posts as chief clerks and in major commanderies.

sentences.zh: 脩起自賤伍，暴致富貴，奢傲無禮，物情所疾。

translations.literal: Xiu had risen from lowly ranks and suddenly attained wealth and nobility; his extravagance, arrogance, and lack of courtesy were detested by all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had risen from lowly ranks and suddenly attained wealth and power; his extravagance, arrogance, and rudeness were hated by all.

sentences.zh: 因其在外，左右或諷糾其罪。

translations.literal: Because he was away from court, those around him sometimes whispered to have his crimes investigated.
translations.idiomatic: While he was away from court, those around him sometimes urged that his crimes be investigated.

sentences.zh: 自其葬父還也，舊寵小薄。

translations.literal: Since his return after burying his father, his former favor had somewhat diminished.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from his father's burial, his former favor had noticeably waned.

sentences.zh: 初，王顯祗附於脩，後因忿鬩，密伺其過，規陷戮之，而脩過短，都不悛防。

translations.literal: Initially Wang Xianzhi attached himself to Xiu, but later, because of a quarrel, he secretly watched for Xiu's mistakes and planned to bring about his execution, while Xiu's own failings were too many and he did nothing to reform or guard against them at all.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wang Xianzhi attached himself to Xiu, but after they quarreled he secretly watched for faults and plotted to have him put to death; Xiu, however, was so flawed that he made no effort to reform or guard himself.

sentences.zh: 顯積其前後愆咎，列脩葬父時路中淫亂不軌，又云與長安人趙僧𢶏謀匿玉印事。

translations.literal: Xian accumulated his earlier and later offenses, listing Xiu's disorderly and illicit conduct on the road while burying his father, and also saying that he had plotted with the Chang'an man Zhao Senggui about concealing the jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: Xian piled up Xiu's earlier and later offenses, citing his licentious and lawless conduct on the road while burying his father, and also alleging that he had conspired with the Chang'an man Zhao Senggui to conceal the jade seal.

sentences.zh: 高肇、甄琛等構成其罪，乃密以聞。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, Zhen Chen, and others framed him for the crime and then secretly reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, Zhen Chen, and others framed him for the offense and secretly reported it.

sentences.zh: 始琛及李憑等曲事於脩，[6]無所不至，懼相連及，爭共糾摘，助攻治之。

translations.literal: At first Zhen and Li Ping and others had flattered and served Xiu in every crooked way,[6] going to any lengths; but fearing they too would be implicated, they competed to denounce him and joined together in attacking and prosecuting him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhen Chen and Li Ping and others had flattered and served Xiu in every possible way,[6] but fearing they would be dragged in as well, they rushed to denounce him and joined forces in prosecuting him.

sentences.zh: 遂乃詔曰：「小人難育、朽棘不彫，長惡不悛，豈容撫養。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued: "A petty man is hard to nurture; rotten thorns cannot be carved. One who persists in evil and does not repent, how can he be indulged and raised up?
translations.idiomatic: An edict then said: "A petty man is hard to nurture; rotten thorns cannot be carved. One who persists in evil and never repents, how can he be tolerated and indulged?

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、領扈左右趙脩，昔在東朝，選充臺皂，幼所經見，長難遺之。

translations.literal: The Gentleman Attendant of the Cavalry, General Who Guards the East, and acting commander of the imperial attendants, Zhao Xiu, when formerly at the Eastern Court, was selected to fill the palace retinue; what was seen in childhood is hard to forget in later years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiu, Gentleman Attendant of the Cavalry, General Who Guards the East, and acting commander of the imperial attendants, was once selected at the Eastern Court to serve in the palace retinue; what one sees in youth is hard to forget later in life.

sentences.zh: 故纂業之初，仍引西禁。

translations.literal: So at the beginning of my succession, I still drew him into the western palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: So at the beginning of my reign, I still brought him into the western guard.

sentences.zh: 雖地微器陋，非所宜採；

translations.literal: Although his background was humble and his abilities crude, he was not the sort to be selected;
translations.idiomatic: Although his origins were lowly and his abilities crude, he was not the sort who should have been chosen.

sentences.zh: 然識早念生，遂陞名級。

translations.literal: Yet because I recognized him early and remembered his service, he was thus raised in rank and status.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because I recognized him early and kept him in mind, he was raised in rank and office.

sentences.zh: 自蒙洗濯，兇昏日甚，驟佞荐驕，恩加輕慢。

translations.literal: From the time he was washed and elevated by grace, his wickedness and stupidity grew worse day by day; though he was repeatedly advanced by flattery, he became arrogant, and when favored, grew contemptuous and disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment he was raised up by favor, his wickedness and folly grew worse by the day. Advanced again and again through flattery, he became arrogant and, under favor, increasingly contemptuous and insolent.

sentences.zh: 不識人倫之體，不悟深淺之方，陵獵王侯，輕觸卿相，門賓巷士，拜叩不接，囂氣豪心，仍懷鄙塞。

translations.literal: He did not understand the proper order among people, nor comprehend the measure of depth and shallowness; he bullied and harried kings and marquises, treated ministers and dukes lightly, and when gate guests and alley scholars came to pay respects, he would not receive their bows and prostrations, retaining a haughty air and arrogant heart, still harboring vulgar meanness.
translations.idiomatic: He did not understand the proper order among people, nor the difference between what was fitting and what was not. He bullied kings and marquises, treated ministers lightly, and when guests or local scholars came to pay respects, he would not even receive their bows. He kept a loud, arrogant bearing and remained coarse and narrow-minded.

sentences.zh: 比聽葬父，侈暴繼聞。

translations.literal: More recently, when I heard of his burying his father, further reports of extravagance and violence followed.
translations.idiomatic: More recently, when I heard of his father's burial, further reports of extravagance and violence followed.

sentences.zh: 居京造宅，殘虐徒旅。

translations.literal: Living in the capital and building houses, he abused and harmed his followers.
translations.idiomatic: While living in the capital and building houses, he brutalized and abused his followers.

sentences.zh: 又廣張形勢，妄生矯託，與雍州人趙僧𢶏等陰相傳納，許受玉印。

translations.literal: He also widely displayed his influence and power, falsely creating pretenses and claims, and secretly exchanged messages with the Yizhou man Zhao Senggui and others, promising to accept the jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: He also made a great display of power, fabricated pretenses and claims, and secretly exchanged messages with the Yongzhou man Zhao Senggui and others, promising to accept the jade seal.

sentences.zh: 不軌不物，日月滋甚。

translations.literal: His conduct grew more and more improper and unruly by the day.
translations.idiomatic: His own conduct grew more and more improper and unruly by the day.

sentences.zh: 朕猶愍其宿隸，每加覆護，而擅威弄勢，侏張不已。

translations.literal: I still pitied his former servile status and repeatedly protected him, but he abused his authority and flaunted his power without end.
translations.idiomatic: I still still pitied his former servile status and repeatedly protected him, but he abused his authority and flaunted his power without end.

sentences.zh: 法家耳目，並求憲網，雖欲捨之，辟實難爽。

translations.literal: The eyes and ears of the law all seek the legal net; even if I want to spare him, the punishment is truly hard to escape.
translations.idiomatic: The law's eyes and ears all keep watch for the net of justice; even if I wanted to spare him, the punishment would be hard to avoid.

sentences.zh: 然楚履既墜，江君徘徊；

translations.literal: Though the Chu shoe has already fallen, Lord Jiang still lingers;
translations.idiomatic: Even though the Chu shoe has already fallen, Lord Jiang still lingers;

sentences.zh: 鍾牛一聲，東向改釁。

translations.literal: at a single sound of the bell ox, the eastward rite is altered.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, at a single sound of the bell ox, the eastward rite is altered.

sentences.zh: 脩雖小人，承侍在昔，極辟之奏，欲加未忍。

translations.literal: Although Xiu is only a petty man, he long attended me, and I am still unwilling to proceed at once to the harshest punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Although Xiu is only a petty man, he long attended me, and I am still unwilling to proceed at once to the harshest punishment.

sentences.zh: 可鞭之一百，徙敦煌為兵。

translations.literal: He should be flogged one hundred strokes and exiled to Dunhuang as a soldier.
translations.idiomatic: He then should be flogged one hundred strokes and exiled to Dunhuang as a soldier.

sentences.zh: 其家宅作徒即仰停罷。

translations.literal: His family home and all work on it should be stopped at once.
translations.idiomatic: His own family home and all work on it should be stopped at once.

sentences.zh: 所親在內者悉令出禁。

translations.literal: All those close to him within the palace should be sent out of the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, All those close to him within the palace should be sent out of the forbidden precincts.

sentences.zh: 朕昧於處物，育茲豺虎，顧尋往謬，有愧臣民，便可時敕申沒，以謝朝野。」

translations.literal: I was blind in dealing with affairs and fostered these tigers and wolves; looking back on my former mistakes, I am ashamed before ministers and commoners alike. Let the proper orders be issued at once to remove him, so as to apologize to court and realm.
translations.idiomatic: I still was blind in dealing with affairs and fostered these tigers and wolves; looking back on my former mistakes, I am ashamed before ministers and commoners alike. Let the proper orders be issued at once to remove him, so as to apologize to court and realm.

sentences.zh: 是日脩詣領軍于勁第與之樗蒲，籌未及畢，而羽林數人相續而至，稱詔呼之。

translations.literal: That day Xiu was at General Yu Jin's house playing pitch-pot with him, and before the game ended several men of the Feathered Forest came one after another, claiming an edict and summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, That day Xiu was at General Yu Jin's house playing pitch-pot with him, and before the game ended several men of the Feathered Forest came one after another, claiming an edict and summoning him.

sentences.zh: 脩驚起隨出，路中執引脩馬詣領軍府。

translations.literal: Xiu rose in alarm and followed them out, and on the road they seized his horse and led him to the office of the Commandant-General.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Xiu rose in alarm and followed them out, and on the road they seized his horse and led him to the office of the Commandant-General.

sentences.zh: 琛與顯監決其罰，先具問事有力者五人更迭鞭之，占令必死。

translations.literal: Zhen and Xian oversaw the punishment, first choosing five strong men familiar with the case to take turns whipping him, with instructions that he must certainly die.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Zhen and Xian oversaw the punishment, first choosing five strong men familiar with the case to take turns whipping him, with instructions that he must certainly die.

sentences.zh: 旨決百鞭，其實三百。

translations.literal: The order fixed the punishment at one hundred strokes, but in fact it was three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The order fixed the punishment at one hundred strokes, but the actual count was three hundred.

sentences.zh: 脩素肥壯，腰背博碩，堪忍楚毒，了不轉動。

translations.literal: Xiu was usually stout and robust, with a broad waist and back, and he could endure pain and torment without even moving.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Xiu was usually stout and robust, with a broad waist and back, and he could endure pain and torment without even moving.

sentences.zh: 鞭訖，即召驛馬，促之令發。

translations.literal: When the whipping was done, they immediately summoned relay horses and hurried him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when the whipping was done, they immediately summoned relay horses and hurried him on his way.

sentences.zh: 出城西門，不自勝舉，縛置鞍中，急驅馳之。

translations.literal: After leaving the west gate of the city, he could no longer support himself, so they bound him in the saddle and drove him on in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, leaving the west gate of the city, he could no longer support himself, so they bound him in the saddle and drove him on in haste.

sentences.zh: 其母妻追隨，不得與語。

translations.literal: His mother and wife followed after him, but were not allowed to speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: His own mother and wife followed after him, but were not allowed to speak with him.

sentences.zh: 行八十里乃死。

translations.literal: He died after traveling eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: He then died after traveling eighty li.

sentences.zh: 初于后之入，脩之力也。

translations.literal: At first, the empress's rise was due to Xiu's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, the empress's rise was due to Xiu's efforts.

sentences.zh: 脩死後，領軍于勁猶追感舊意，經恤其家，自餘朝士昔相宗承者，悉棄絕之，示己之疏遠焉。

translations.literal: After Xiu's death, Commander Yu Jin still remembered their old connection and continued to look after his family; the other court officials who had once respected and served him all cut ties, showing their distance.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, Xiu's death, Commander Yu Jin still remembered their old connection and continued to look after his family; the other court officials who had once respected and served him all cut ties, showing their distance.

sentences.zh: 茹皓，字禽奇，舊吳人也。

translations.literal: Ru Hao, courtesy name Qinqi, was an old resident of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Ru Hao, courtesy name Qinqi, was an old resident of Wu.

sentences.zh: 父讓之，本名要，隨劉駿巴陵王休若為將，至彭城。

translations.literal: His father, Rangzhi, originally named Yao, followed Liu Jun and Prince Xiuruo of Baling as a general, and came to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His own father, Rangzhi, originally named Yao, followed Liu Jun and Prince Xiuruo of Baling as a general, and came to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 是時南土飢亂，遂寓居淮陽上黨。

translations.literal: At that time the southern lands were suffering famine and disorder, so they took up residence in Huaiyang and Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, that time the southern lands were suffering famine and disorder, so they took up residence in Huaiyang and Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 皓年十五六，為縣金曹吏，有姿貌，謹惠。

translations.literal: When he was fifteen or sixteen, Hao served as a clerk in the county finance office; he had a pleasing appearance and was careful and obliging.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when he was fifteen or sixteen, Hao served as a clerk in the county finance office; he had a pleasing appearance and was careful and obliging.

sentences.zh: 南徐州刺史沈陵見而善之，自隨入洛陽，舉充高祖白衣左右。

translations.literal: Seeing him, Shen Ling, Inspector of South Xu Province, approved of him, brought him along to Luoyang, and recommended him for placement among Gaozu's plainclothes attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Seeing him, Shen Ling, Inspector of South Xu Province, approved of him, brought him along to Luoyang, and recommended him for placement among Gaozu's plainclothes attendants.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐祚，皓侍直禁中，稍被寵接。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Hao served on duty in the forbidden palace and gradually gained favor and access.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Hao served on duty in the forbidden palace and gradually gained favor and access.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗拜山陵，路中欲引與同車，皓奮衣將昇，黃門侍郎元匡切諫乃止。

translations.literal: Once Emperor Shizong was making a pilgrimage to the mountain mausoleums, and on the road he wanted to have Hao ride in the same carriage; Hao shook out his robes and was about to climb aboard, but only when Yellow Gate Gentleman Yuan Kuang urgently remonstrated did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Once Emperor Shizong was making a pilgrimage to the mountain mausoleums, and on the road he wanted to have Hao ride in the same carriage; Hao shook out his robes and was about to climb aboard, but only when Yellow Gate Gentleman Yuan Kuang urgently remonstrated did he stop.

sentences.zh: 及世宗親政，皓眷賚日隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong personally took control of government, Hao's favor and rewards increased day by day.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when Emperor Shizong personally took control of government, Hao's favor and rewards increased day by day.

sentences.zh: 又以馬圈之勞，當擬補員外將軍。

translations.literal: He was also to be considered for appointment as an Assistant General because of the service he had rendered at the horse enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: He then was also to be considered for appointment as an Assistant General because of the service he had rendered at the horse enclosure.

sentences.zh: 時趙脩亦被幸，妬害之，求出皓為外守。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Xiu was also favored, and out of jealousy he sought to have Hao sent out as a provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, that time Zhao Xiu was also favored, and out of jealousy he sought to have Hao sent out as a provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 皓亦慮見危禍，不樂內官，遂超授濮陽太守，加厲威將軍。

translations.literal: Hao himself also feared danger and misfortune and was not fond of an inner-court post, so he was exceptionally promoted to Prefect of Puyang and given the title General of Awe-Inspiring Might.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Hao himself also feared danger and misfortune and was not fond of an inner-court post, so he was exceptionally promoted to Prefect of Puyang and given the title General of Awe-Inspiring Might.

sentences.zh: 其父因皓訟理舊勳，先除兗州陽平太守，賜以子爵。

translations.literal: Because Hao petitioned on behalf of his father's old service, his father was first appointed Prefect of Yangping in Yanzhou and granted the title of viscount.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason, Hao petitioned on behalf of his father's old service, his father was first appointed Prefect of Yangping in Yanzhou and granted the title of viscount.

sentences.zh: 父子剖符名邦，郡境相接，皓忻然於去內，不以疏外為戚。

translations.literal: Father and son each received a fief in a famous commandery, and the two commandery territories touched; Hao was delighted to be leaving the inner court and did not regard being kept away from it as a sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Father and son each received a fief in a famous commandery, and the two commandery territories touched; Hao was delighted to be leaving the inner court and did not regard being kept away from it as a sorrow.

sentences.zh: 及趙脩等敗，竟獲全免。

translations.literal: When Zhao Xiu and the others fell from power, he ultimately escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when Zhao Xiu and the others fell from power, he ultimately escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 雖起微細，為守乃清簡寡事。

translations.literal: Though he had risen from obscurity, as a governor he was plain and restrained, with few affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Even though he had risen from obscurity, as a governor he was plain and restrained, with few affairs.

sentences.zh: 世宗幸鄴講武，皓啟求朝趨，解郡，授左中郎將，領直閤。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong went to Ye to lecture on military matters, Hao petitioned to attend the court procession, resigned his commandery, and was appointed Left Middle Guard General, in charge of the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when Emperor Shizong went to Ye to lecture on military matters, Hao petitioned to attend the court procession, resigned his commandery, and was appointed Left Middle Guard General, in charge of the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 寵待如前。

translations.literal: His favor and treatment were as before.
translations.idiomatic: His own favor and treatment were as before.

sentences.zh: 皓既官達，自云本出雁門，雁門人諂附者乃因薦皓於司徒，請為肆州大中正。

translations.literal: Once Hao was established in office, he claimed that he had originally come from Yanmen, and men from Yanmen who fawned on him then recommended him to the Minister over the Masses, asking that he be made Grand Arbiter of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Once Hao was established in office, he claimed that he had originally come from Yanmen, and men from Yanmen who fawned on him then recommended him to the Minister over the Masses, asking that he be made Grand Arbiter of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 府、省以聞，詔特依許。

translations.literal: The central office and ministries reported it, and the edict specially granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The central office and ministries reported it, and the edict specially approved it.

sentences.zh: 遷驃騎將軍，領華林諸作。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Cavalry and placed in charge of the various works of Hualin.
translations.idiomatic: He then was transferred to General of Cavalry and placed in charge of the various works of Hualin.

sentences.zh: 皓性微工巧，多所興立。

translations.literal: Hao had a slight talent for craftsmanship and created many constructions.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Hao had a slight talent for craftsmanship and created many constructions.

sentences.zh: 為山於天淵池西，採掘北邙及南山佳石。

translations.literal: He built an artificial mountain west of Tianyuan Pond, quarrying fine stone from Beiman and the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He then built an artificial mountain west of Tianyuan Pond, quarrying fine stone from Beiman and the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 徙竹汝潁，羅蒔其間；

translations.literal: He moved bamboo from the Ru and Ying rivers and planted it thickly among the grounds;
translations.idiomatic: He then moved bamboo from the Ru and Ying rivers and planted it thickly among the grounds;

sentences.zh: 經構樓館，列於上下。

translations.literal: he built towers and halls arranged in tiers above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, he built towers and halls arranged in tiers above and below.

sentences.zh: 樹草栽木，頗有野致。

translations.literal: He planted grasses and trees, and the place acquired a somewhat rustic charm.
translations.idiomatic: He then planted grasses and trees, and the place acquired a somewhat rustic charm.

sentences.zh: 世宗心悅之，以時臨幸。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong was pleased with it and would occasionally come in person to visit.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Emperor Shizong was pleased with it and would occasionally come in person to visit.

sentences.zh: 遷冠軍將軍、仍驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Champion Guard and remained General of the Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He then was transferred to General of the Champion Guard and remained General of the Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 皓貴寵日升，關與政事。

translations.literal: Hao's favor and influence rose day by day, and he became involved in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Hao's favor and influence rose day by day, and he became involved in government affairs.

sentences.zh: 太傅、北海王詳以下咸祗憚附之。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor, the Prince of Beihai, Xiang, and all below him respectfully feared and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor, the Prince of Beihai, Xiang, and everyone below him treated him with deference and attached themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 皓弟年尚二十，擢補員外郎。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother, though not yet twenty, was promoted to fill an Assistant Secretary post.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Hao's younger brother, though not yet twenty, was promoted to fill an Assistant Secretary post.

sentences.zh: 皓娶僕射高肇從妹，於世宗為從母。

translations.literal: Hao married the paternal cousin of Vice Director Gao Zhao; to Emperor Shizong, she was a maternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Hao married the paternal cousin of Vice Director Gao Zhao; to Emperor Shizong, she was a maternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 迎納之日，詳親詣之，禮以馬物。

translations.literal: On the day of the wedding, Xiang personally came to the house and presented horses and other gifts as a courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: On that occasion, the day of the wedding, Xiang personally came to the house and presented horses and other gifts as a courtesy.

sentences.zh: 皓又為弟聘安豐王延明妹，延明耻非舊流，不許。

translations.literal: Hao also arranged for his brother to marry the younger sister of Prince Yanming of Anfeng, but Yanming, ashamed that Hao was not of the old established line, refused.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Hao also arranged for his brother to marry the younger sister of Prince Yanming of Anfeng, but Yanming, ashamed that Hao was not of the old established line, refused.

sentences.zh: 詳勸強之云：「欲覓官職，如何不與茹皓婚姻也？

translations.literal: Xiang urged him on, saying: "If you want to seek office, how can you not marry into Ru Hao's family?"
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Xiang urged him on, saying: "If you want to seek office, how can you not marry into Ru Hao's family?"

sentences.zh: 」延明乃從焉。

translations.literal: Yanming then complied.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Yanming then complied.

sentences.zh: 皓頗敏慧，折節下人。

translations.literal: Hao was quite quick and intelligent, and he lowered himself to meet others on their terms.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Hao was quite quick and intelligent, and he lowered himself to meet others on their terms.

sentences.zh: 而潛自經營，陰有納受，貨產盈積。

translations.literal: But in secret he managed affairs and privately accepted gifts, and his wealth piled up day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, But in secret he managed affairs and privately accepted gifts, and his wealth piled up day by day.

sentences.zh: 起宅宮西，朝貴弗之及也。

translations.literal: He built a residence west of the palace, beyond the reach of the court nobility.
translations.idiomatic: He then built a residence west of the palace, beyond the reach of the court nobility.

sentences.zh: 是時世宗雖親萬務，皓率常居內，留宿不還，傳可門下奏事。

translations.literal: At that time, although Emperor Shizong handled all affairs personally, Hao generally stayed inside, slept there without returning, and had memorials passed through the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, that time, although Emperor Shizong handled all affairs personally, Hao generally stayed inside, slept there without returning, and had memorials passed through the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 未幾，轉光祿少卿，意殊不已，方欲陳馬圈從先帝之勞，更希進舉。

translations.literal: Before long, he was transferred to Junior Minister of Imperial Entertainments, and he was still unsatisfied, hoping to cite his service at the horse enclosure under the former emperor and seek further advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, long, he was transferred to Junior Minister of Imperial Entertainments, and he was still unsatisfied, hoping to cite his service at the horse enclosure under the former emperor and seek further advancement.

sentences.zh: 初，脩、皓之寵，北海王詳皆附納之。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhao Xiu and Hao were favored, Prince Beihai Xiang all attached himself to them.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Zhao Xiu and Hao were favored, Prince Beihai Xiang all attached himself to them.

sentences.zh: 又直閤將軍劉冑本為詳所薦，常感詳恩，密相承望，並共來往。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Gates, Liu Zhou, had originally been recommended by Xiang, and always remembered Xiang's favor, secretly corresponding and associating with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Palace Gates, Liu Zhou, had originally been recommended by Xiang, and always remembered Xiang's favor, secretly corresponding and keeping up relations with him.

sentences.zh: 高肇素疾諸王，常規陷害，既知詳與皓等交關相昵，乃構之世宗，云皓等將有異謀。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao long resented the princes and often schemed to frame and ruin them; once he learned that Xiang was closely friendly with Hao and the others, he plotted against them before Emperor Shizong, saying that Hao and the others were preparing some different scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Gao Zhao long resented the princes and often schemed to frame and ruin them; once he learned that Xiang was closely friendly with Hao and the others, he plotted against them before Emperor Shizong, saying that Hao and the others were preparing some different scheme.

sentences.zh: 世宗乃召中尉崔亮令奏皓、冑、常季賢、陳掃靜四人擅勢納賄及私亂諸事，即日執皓等皆詣南臺。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong then summoned the Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang and ordered him to report Hao, Zhou, Chang Jixian, and Chen Saojing for abusing power, taking bribes, and private misconduct; that same day Hao and the others were seized and all taken to the Southern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Emperor Shizong then summoned the Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang and ordered him to report Hao, Zhou, Chang Jixian, and Chen Saojing for abusing power, taking bribes, and private misconduct; that same day Hao and the others were seized and all taken to the Southern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 翌日，奏處罪，其晚就家殺之。

translations.literal: The next day, the charges were resolved, and that evening they were killed at home.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, the case was settled, and that evening they were killed at home.

sentences.zh: 皓妻被髮出堂，哭而迎皓。

translations.literal: Hao's wife came out into the hall with her hair unbound, weeping as she greeted Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Hao's wife came out into the hall with her hair unbound, weeping as she greeted Hao.

sentences.zh: 皓徑入哭別，食椒而死。

translations.literal: Hao went straight in, wept his farewell, and died after eating pepper.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Hao went straight in, wept his farewell, and died after eating pepper.

sentences.zh: 皓子懷朗，仕至南青州刺史。

translations.literal: Hao's son Huailang rose to be Inspector of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Hao's son Huailang rose to be Inspector of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 興和初，以罪賜死，子姪徙邊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xinghe era, he was executed for his crimes, and his sons and nephews were exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the beginning of the Xinghe era, he was executed for his crimes, and his sons and nephews were exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 冑，字元孫，河間人。

translations.literal: Zhou, courtesy name Yuansun, was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Zhou, courtesy name Yuansun, was a man of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 始為北海王詳所舉。

translations.literal: He was first recommended by Prince of Beihai Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then was first recommended by Prince of Beihai Xiang.

sentences.zh: 六輔時，出守本郡，與皓俱赴鄴宮講武，亦自乞留。

translations.literal: During the period of the Six Auxiliaries, he was sent out to guard his native commandery, and when he and Hao went to the Ye palace for military exercises, he also petitioned to remain.
translations.idiomatic: During that time, the period of the Six Auxiliaries, he was sent out to guard his native commandery, and when he and Hao went to the Ye palace for military exercises, he also petitioned to remain.

sentences.zh: 至洛，久不敍用。

translations.literal: After he reached Luoyang, he went a long time without being employed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, he reached Luoyang, he went a long time without being employed.

sentences.zh: 詳又為啟，晚乃拜將軍直閤。

translations.literal: Xiang again petitioned on his behalf, and only later was he appointed as General and Director of the Palace Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Xiang again petitioned on his behalf, and only later was he appointed as General and Director of the Palace Gates.

sentences.zh: 季賢起於主馬，世宗初好騎乘，因是獲寵。

translations.literal: Ji Xian rose from the stable office; when Emperor Shizong first took up riding, he won favor because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Ji Xian rose from the stable office; when Emperor Shizong first took up riding, he won favor because of this.

sentences.zh: 位至殿中將軍、司藥丞，仍主廐閑。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Palace General and Assistant Commissioner of Medicines, while still managing the stables.
translations.idiomatic: He then reached the post of Palace General and Assistant Commissioner of Medicines, while still managing the stables.

sentences.zh: 與茹皓通知庶事，勢望漸隆。

translations.literal: He communicated with Ru Hao about all affairs, and his influence and standing gradually rose.
translations.idiomatic: He then communicated with Ru Hao about all affairs, and his influence and standing gradually rose.

sentences.zh: 引其兄為朝請、直寢，娶武昌王鑒妹。

translations.literal: He had his elder brother appointed to Court Audience Attendant and Palace Chamberlain, and married a sister of Prince Jian of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He then had his elder brother appointed to Court Audience Attendant and Palace Chamberlain, and married a sister of Prince Jian of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 季賢又將娶洛州刺史元拔女，並結託帝戚以為榮援云。

translations.literal: Ji Xian also planned to marry the daughter of Yuan Ba, Inspector of Luzhou, and in every case he tied himself to imperial kin as a source of honor and support.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Ji Xian also planned to marry the daughter of Yuan Ba, Inspector of Luzhou, and in every case he tied himself to imperial kin as a source of honor and support.

sentences.zh: 掃靜、徐義恭，並彭城舊營人。

translations.literal: Saojing and Xu Yigong were both old men from the Pengcheng camp.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Saojing and Xu Yigong were both old men from the Pengcheng camp.

sentences.zh: 掃靜能為世宗典櫛梳，義恭善執衣服，並以巧便，旦夕居中，愛幸相侔，官敍不異。

translations.literal: Saojing was able to style Emperor Shizong's hair and comb it, and Yigong was good at dressing him; both were clever and handy, stayed in the inner court from morning to night, were equally favored, and held no different offices.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Saojing was able to style Emperor Shizong's hair and comb it, and Yigong was good at dressing him; both were clever and handy, stayed in the inner court from morning to night, were equally favored, and held no different offices.

sentences.zh: 掃靜妻，義恭姊也，情相遺薄，室家不諧。

translations.literal: Saojing's wife was Yigong's elder sister, and the two had grown cold toward each other, so the household was not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Saojing's wife was Yigong's elder sister, and the two had grown cold toward each other, so the household was not harmonious.

sentences.zh: 義恭恒忿恨之，親經世宗，訴其欺侮。

translations.literal: Yigong was constantly resentful of this and personally went to Emperor Shizong to complain of their mistreatment.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Yigong was constantly resentful of this and personally went to Emperor Shizong to complain of their mistreatment.

sentences.zh: 世宗以其左右，兩護之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because they were close attendants, protected both of them.
translations.idiomatic: Because they were both close attendants, the emperor protected them both.

sentences.zh: 二人皆承奉茹皓，亦並加接眷，而掃靜偏為親密，與皓常在左右，略不歸休。

translations.literal: The two both served Ru Hao and were likewise treated with favor, but Saojing was especially close to him; he stayed with Hao around the emperor and hardly ever returned to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Both served Ru Hao and were likewise favored, but Saojing was especially close to him; he stayed with Hao around the emperor and hardly ever went back to rest.

sentences.zh: 皓敗，掃靜亦死於家。

translations.literal: After Hao fell, Saojing also died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, Hao fell, Saojing also died at home.

sentences.zh: 義恭小心謹慎，謙退少語。

translations.literal: Yigong was careful and cautious, deferential and sparing of words.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Yigong was careful and cautious, deferential and sparing of words.

sentences.zh: 皓等死後，彌見幸信，長侍左右，典掌祕密。

translations.literal: After Hao and the others died, he was even more trusted and believed, constantly attending the emperor and managing secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, Hao and the others died, he was even more trusted and believed, constantly attending the emperor and managing secret affairs.

sentences.zh: 世宗不豫，義恭晝夜扶侍，崩于懷中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong fell ill, Yigong attended him day and night, and the emperor died in his arms.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when Emperor Shizong fell ill, Yigong attended him day and night, and the emperor died in his arms.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨政，義恭諂附元叉，又有淫宴，[7]多在其宅。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager Ling governed, Yigong flattered Yuan Cha and also held licentious banquets [7], often at his house.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager Ling governed, Yigong flattered Yuan Cha and held licentious banquets [7], often at his house.

sentences.zh: 為嘗藥次御，出為東秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed to taste medicine, then sent out as Inspector of Eastern Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then was appointed to taste medicine, then sent out as Inspector of Eastern Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 建義後，歷內外顯職。

translations.literal: After the Jianyi period began, he held prominent posts both inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, the Jianyi period began, he held prominent posts both inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 武定初，卒於驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wuding era, he died while serving as Grand General of the Cavalry and Left Grand Master of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the beginning of the Wuding era, he died while serving as Grand General of the Cavalry and Left Grand Master of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 趙邕，字令和，自云南陽人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yong, courtesy name Linghe, claimed to be a native of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Zhao Yong, courtesy name Linghe, claimed to be a native of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 潔白明髭眉，曉了恭敏。

translations.literal: He had a clean complexion, bright beard and eyebrows, and was quick to understand, respectful, and diligent.
translations.idiomatic: He then had a clean complexion, bright beard and eyebrows, and was quick to understand, respectful, and diligent.

sentences.zh: 司空李沖之貴寵也，邕以少年端謹，出入其家，頗給按磨奔走之役。

translations.literal: When Li Chong was rich and favored, Yong, though still young and upright, came and went in his household and often did various errands and menial tasks.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when Li Chong was rich and favored, Yong, though still young and upright, came and went in his household and often did various errands and menial tasks.

sentences.zh: 沖亦深加接念，令與諸子游處。

translations.literal: Chong also treated him with deep favor and had him keep company with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Chong also treated him with deep favor and had him keep company with his sons.

sentences.zh: 人有束帶謁於沖者，時託之以自通。

translations.literal: When someone came to pay respects to Chong in formal dress, he would sometimes rely on Yong to introduce them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when someone came to pay respects to Chong in formal dress, he would sometimes rely on Yong to introduce them.

sentences.zh: 高祖太和中，給事左右，至殿中監。

translations.literal: During Emperor Gaozu's Taihe reign, he served among the attendants and rose to Palace Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: During that time, Emperor Gaozu's Taihe reign, he served among the attendants and rose to Palace Superintendent.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位及親政，猶居本任。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong came to the throne and took personal control of government, he still remained in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Emperor Shizong came to the throne and took personal control of government, he still remained in his original post.

sentences.zh: 微與趙脩結為宗援，然亦不甚相附也。

translations.literal: He had only a tenuous clan connection with Zhao Xiu, and though the two were allied, they were not especially close.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he had only a tenuous clan connection with Zhao Xiu, and though the two were allied, they were not especially close.

sentences.zh: 邕稍遷至殿中將軍，猶帶監職。

translations.literal: Yong was gradually promoted to Palace General, while still holding the supervisory post.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, yong was gradually promoted to Palace General, while still holding the supervisory post.

sentences.zh: 邕父怡，太和中歷郢州刺史，停家久之，以邕寵召拜太常少卿。

translations.literal: Yong's father Yi served as Inspector of Yingzhou during the Taihe reign; after staying at home for a long time, he was summoned because of Yong's favor and appointed Junior Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, yong's father Yi served as Inspector of Yingzhou during the Taihe reign; after staying at home for a long time, he was summoned because of Yong's favor and appointed Junior Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尋為荊州大中正，出除征虜將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Grand Arbiter of Jingzhou and then sent out as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, soon he was made Grand Arbiter of Jingzhou and then sent out as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 怡乃致其母喪，葬於宛城之南，趙氏舊墟。

translations.literal: Yi then arranged his mother's funeral and buried her south of Wancheng, at the old Zhao family site.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, yi then arranged his mother's funeral and buried her south of Wancheng, at the old Zhao family site.

sentences.zh: 以老乞解州任，遷拜光祿大夫，轉金紫光祿。

translations.literal: Because of his age, he asked to be relieved of his provincial post and was promoted to Grand Master of Imperial Entertainments, then transferred to Golden Purple Grand Master of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, because of his age, he asked to be relieved of his provincial post and was promoted to Grand Master of Imperial Entertainments, then transferred to Golden Purple Grand Master of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮東將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously honored as General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when he died, he was posthumously honored as General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗每出入郊廟，脩恒以常侍、侍中陪乘，而邕兼奉車都尉，執轡同載。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Shizong went to the suburbs or ancestral temples, Xiu always rode with him as attendant, while Yong, as Commandant of the Chariot, held the reins and rode in the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, whenever Emperor Shizong went to the suburbs or ancestral temples, Xiu always rode with him as attendant, while Yong, as Commandant of the Chariot, held the reins and rode in the same carriage.

sentences.zh: 時人竊論，號為「二趙」。

translations.literal: People at the time privately called them the "two Zhaos."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, people at the time privately called them the "two Zhaos."

sentences.zh: 以趙出南陽，徙屬荊，邕轉給事中、南陽中正，以父為荊州大中正，乃罷。

translations.literal: Because Zhao was from Nanyang and had been moved to Jing, Yong was transferred to Assistant Clerk and Arbiter of Nanyang; when his father became Grand Arbiter of Jingzhou, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, because Zhao was from Nanyang and had been moved to Jing, Yong was transferred to Assistant Clerk and Arbiter of Nanyang; when his father became Grand Arbiter of Jingzhou, he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 轉長兼散騎侍郎、領左右、直長，出入禁中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Chief Gentleman Attendant, in charge of the Left, and Palace Director, going in and out of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was transferred to Acting Chief Gentleman Attendant, in charge of the Left, and Palace Director, going in and out of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 復為荊州大中正。

translations.literal: He was again made Grand Arbiter of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was again made Grand Arbiter of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 邕弟尚，中書舍人，出除南陽太守。

translations.literal: Yong's younger brother Shang, a secretary in the Secretariat, was sent out as Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, yong's younger brother Shang, a secretary in the Secretariat, was sent out as Administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 怡辭荊州也，尚求解郡，與父俱還。

translations.literal: When Yi resigned from Jingzhou, Shang also asked to be relieved of his commandery post and returned home with his father.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Yi resigned from Jingzhou, Shang also asked to be relieved of his commandery post and returned home with his father.

sentences.zh: 未至京師，逆除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Before reaching the capital, he was preemptively appointed Infantry Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, before reaching the capital, he was preemptively appointed Infantry Colonel.

sentences.zh: 邕祖嶽舊葬代京，喪自平城還葬南陽，贈平遠將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Yong's grandfather Yue had long been buried in the old capital of Dai; when the family returned his coffin from Pingcheng for burial in Nanyang, he was posthumously honored as General of Pacifying Distance and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, yong's grandfather Yue had long been buried in the old capital of Dai; when the family returned his coffin from Pingcheng for burial in Nanyang, he was posthumously honored as General of Pacifying Distance and Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，邕兼給事黃門，俄轉太府卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong died, Yong was concurrently Palace Attendant and Yellow Gate Gentleman, and before long was transferred to Minister of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Emperor Shizong died, Yong was concurrently Palace Attendant and Yellow Gate Gentleman, and before long was transferred to Minister of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 出除平北將軍、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州貪縱。

translations.literal: While in the province, he was greedy and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, while in the province, he was greedy and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 與范陽盧氏為婚，女父早亡，其叔許之，而母不從。

translations.literal: He married into the Fanyang Lu clan, but the girl's father died early; her uncle agreed, but her mother refused.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he married into the Fanyang Lu clan, but the girl's father died early; her uncle agreed, but her mother refused.

sentences.zh: 母北平陽氏攜女至家藏避規免，邕乃拷掠陽叔，遂至於死。

translations.literal: Her mother, of the Yang clan of Beiping, hid the girl at home to avoid the marriage, so Yong had the Yang uncle beaten, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, her mother, of the Yang clan of Beiping, hid the girl at home to avoid the marriage, so Yong had the Yang uncle beaten, and he died.

sentences.zh: 陽氏訴冤，臺遣中散大夫孫景安研檢事狀，邕坐處死，會赦得免，猶當除名。

translations.literal: The Yang clan complained of the injustice, and the court sent Senior Grand Master Sun Jing'an to investigate. Yong was sentenced to death, but escaped because of a general amnesty, though he still should have been struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the Yang clan complained of the injustice, and the court sent Senior Grand Master Sun Jing'an to investigate. Yong was sentenced to death, but escaped because of a general amnesty, though he still should have been struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 自理經年，臨淮王彧時為廷尉，久不斷決。

translations.literal: He defended himself for more than a year; at the time, Prince Yu of Linhuai served as Minister of Justice, and the case remained undecided for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he defended himself for more than a year; at the time, Prince Yu of Linhuai served as Minister of Justice, and the case remained undecided for a long time.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Xiaochang era.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he died at the beginning of the Xiaochang era.

sentences.zh: 侯剛，字乾之，河南洛陽人，其先代人也。

translations.literal: Hou Gang, courtesy name Qianzhi, was a native of Luoyang in Henan; his ancestors were from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, hou Gang, courtesy name Qianzhi, was a native of Luoyang in Henan; his ancestors were from Dai.

sentences.zh: 本出寒微，少以善於鼎爼，進餁出入。

translations.literal: Born into humble poverty, he was young and good at handling the cauldrons and serving food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, born into humble poverty, he was young and good at handling the cauldrons and serving food and drink.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜中散，累遷冗從僕射、嘗食典御。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was appointed Zhongsan and, through repeated promotions, became Deputy Director of the Miscellaneous Attendants and Director of Tasting Food.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, after a long while, he was appointed Zhongsan and, through repeated promotions, became Deputy Director of the Miscellaneous Attendants and Director of Tasting Food.

sentences.zh: 世宗以其質直，賜名剛焉。

translations.literal: Seeing his straightforward nature, Emperor Shizong gave him the name Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, seeing his straightforward nature, Emperor Shizong gave him the name Gang.

sentences.zh: 稍遷奉車都尉、右中郎將、領刀劍左右，加游擊將軍、城門校尉。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Commandant of the Chariot, Right Gentleman General, in charge of the Sword Bearers, and also added General of the Valiant Cavalry and Palace Gate Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was gradually promoted to Commandant of the Chariot, Right Gentleman General, in charge of the Sword Bearers, and also added General of the Valiant Cavalry and Palace Gate Commandant.

sentences.zh: 遷武衞將軍，仍領典御，又加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of the Guard and still kept the office of Director of Tasting Food; he was also made Gentleman Attendant of the Regular Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was promoted to General of the Guard and still kept the office of Director of Tasting Food; he was also made Gentleman Attendant of the Regular Audience.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太和之季，蟻寇侵疆，先皇於不豫之中，命師出討。

translations.literal: In the later years of Taihe, petty bandits invaded the borders. The Former Emperor, while indisposed, ordered troops to go out and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in the later years of Taihe, petty bandits invaded the borders. The Former Emperor, while indisposed, ordered troops to go out and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 撫戎暴露，觸御乖和，朕屬當監國，弗獲隨侍，而左右服事，唯藉忠勤。

translations.literal: While pacifying the army in the open and exposed to the elements, he offended the emperor's health and harmony. Since I happened to be acting as regent and could not accompany and attend him, the attendants and service staff could rely only on loyalty and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, while pacifying the army in the open and exposed to the elements, he offended the emperor's health and harmony. Since I happened to be acting as regent and could not accompany and attend him, the attendants and service staff could rely only on loyalty and diligence.

sentences.zh: 剛於違和之中，辛勤行餁。

translations.literal: Gang, while the emperor was unwell, worked hard to carry the food service.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, gang, while the emperor was unwell, worked hard to carry the food service.

sentences.zh: 追遠錄誠，宜先推敍。

translations.literal: In recognition of such remote service and sincerity, promotion should come first.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in recognition of such remote service and sincerity, promotion should come first.

sentences.zh: 其以剛為右衞大將軍。

translations.literal: Therefore appoint Gang as Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, therefore appoint Gang as Grand General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 」[8]後領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Later he was made Palace Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, later he was made Palace Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，剛與侍中崔光迎肅宗於東宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong died, Gang and Palace Attendant Cui Guang welcomed Emperor Suzong at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Emperor Shizong died, Gang and Palace Attendant Cui Guang welcomed Emperor Suzong at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 尋除衞尉卿，封武陽縣開國侯，邑千二百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of the Guards and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang County, with 1,200 households.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, soon he was appointed Minister of the Guards and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang County, with 1,200 households.

sentences.zh: 俄為侍中、撫軍將軍、恒州大中正。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Palace Attendant, General of the Pacification Army, and Grand Arbiter of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, before long he was made Palace Attendant, General of the Pacification Army, and Grand Arbiter of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷衞將軍，表讓侍中，詔不許。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of the Guards; he memorialized asking to decline the Palace Attendant post, but the edict did not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was promoted to General of the Guards; he memorialized asking to decline the Palace Attendant post, but the edict did not allow it.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公，以給侍之勞，加賞散伯。

translations.literal: He was advanced to duke, and because of his service attending the emperor, was additionally granted the rank of Sanbo.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was advanced to duke, and because of his service attending the emperor, was additionally granted the rank of Sanbo.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，除左衞將軍，餘官如故。

translations.literal: At the start of Xiaping, he was made General of the Left Guard, while his other offices remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, at the start of Xiaping, he was made General of the Left Guard, while his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 侍中游肇出為相州。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant You Zao was sent out as Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, palace Attendant You Zao was sent out as Inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 剛言於靈太后曰：「昔高氏擅權，游肇抗衡不屈，先帝所知，四海同見，而出牧一藩，未盡其美，宜還引入，以輔聖主。

translations.literal: Gang said to Empress Dowager Ling: "In former days the Gao clan monopolized power, yet You Zao opposed them and did not bend. This was known to the former emperor and seen by all under heaven, but he was sent out to govern a province, which did not fully use his talents. He should be brought back to assist the sagely ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, gang said to Empress Dowager Ling: "In former days the Gao clan monopolized power, yet You Zao opposed them and did not bend. This was known to the former emperor and seen by all under heaven, but he was sent out to govern a province, which did not fully use his talents. He should be brought back to assist the sagely ruler."

sentences.zh: 」太后善之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager approved.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the empress dowager approved.

sentences.zh: 剛寵任既隆，江陽王繼、尚書長孫稚皆以女妻其子。

translations.literal: Once Gang's favor and appointment had grown great, Prince Jiangyang Ji and Shangshu Changsun Zhi both married their daughters to his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, once Gang's favor and appointment had grown great, Prince Jiangyang Ji and Shangshu Changsun Zhi both married their daughters to his sons.

sentences.zh: 司空、任城王澄以其起由膳宰，頗竊侮之，云：「此近為我舉食。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works, Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, secretly looked down on him because he had risen from the kitchen, and said, "This fellow recently fetched my food."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the Minister of Works, Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, secretly looked down on him because he had risen from the kitchen, and said, "This fellow recently fetched my food."

sentences.zh: 」然公坐對集，敬遇不虧。

translations.literal: Even so, in public meetings and official gatherings, he was treated respectfully without any diminution.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, even so, in public meetings and official gatherings, he was treated respectfully without any diminution.

sentences.zh: 後剛坐掠殺試射羽林，為御史中尉元匡所彈，廷尉處剛大辟。

translations.literal: Later, Gang was impeached by the imperial censor Yuan Kuang for having beaten and killed trial archers of the Feathered Forest, and the Judicial Office sentenced Gang to death.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, later, Gang was impeached by the imperial censor Yuan Kuang for having beaten and killed trial archers of the Feathered Forest, and the Judicial Office sentenced Gang to death.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、任城王澄為之言於靈太后，侯剛歷仕前朝，事有可取，纖芥之疵，未宜便致於法。

translations.literal: The Shangshu Ling, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, spoke to Empress Dowager Ling on his behalf, saying that Hou Gang had served through the former court and had merits worth considering, and that a minor blemish should not immediately bring legal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the Shangshu Ling, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, spoke to Empress Dowager Ling on his behalf, saying that Hou Gang had served through the former court and had merits worth considering, and that a minor blemish should not immediately bring legal punishment.

sentences.zh: 靈太后乃引見廷尉卿裴延儁、少卿袁翻於宣光殿，問曰：「剛因公事掠人，邂逅致死，律文不坐。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then summoned the Judicial Court Minister Pei Yanjuan and Junior Minister Yuan Fan to Xuanguang Hall and asked: "Gang, in the course of official business, had people beaten and they happened to die; by the code, this is not punishable.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the Empress Dowager then summoned the Judicial Court Minister Pei Yanjuan and Junior Minister Yuan Fan to Xuanguang Hall and asked: "Gang, in the course of official business, had people beaten and they happened to die; by the code, this is not punishable.

sentences.zh: 卿處其大辟，竟何所依？

translations.literal: On what basis, then, did you sentence him to death?
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, on what basis, then, did you sentence him to death?

sentences.zh: 」翻對曰：「案律邂逅不坐者，謂情理已露，而隱避不引，必須箠撻，取其款言，謂撾撻以理之類。

translations.literal: Fan replied: "Under the code, the rule that someone is not punished in an unexpected case refers to situations in which the facts are already clear, but the person conceals them and refuses to confess, so whipping is required in order to extract a truthful statement; that is, the class of cases in which blows are used to obtain the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, fan replied: "Under the code, the rule that someone is not punished in an unexpected case refers to situations in which the facts are already clear, but the person conceals them and refuses to confess, so whipping is required in order to extract a truthful statement; that is, the class of cases in which blows are used to obtain the facts.

sentences.zh: 至於此人，問則具首，正宜依犯結案，不應橫加箠扑。

translations.literal: As for this man, when questioned he fully confessed, so he should simply have been judged on the offense itself, and not subjected to arbitrary beating.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, as for this man, when questioned he fully confessed, so he should simply have been judged on the offense itself, and not subjected to arbitrary beating.

sentences.zh: 兼剛口唱打殺，撾築非理，本有殺心，事非邂逅。

translations.literal: Moreover, Gang himself shouted for the beating, and the blows and pounding were unjustified; he already had murderous intent, so this was not an unexpected case.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, moreover, Gang himself shouted for the beating, and the blows and pounding were unjustified; he already had murderous intent, so this was not an unexpected case.

sentences.zh: 處之大辟，未乖憲典。

translations.literal: Sentencing him to death does not violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, sentencing him to death does not violate the law.

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「卿等且還，當別有判。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "You two may go for now; there will be another judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the empress dowager said, "You two may go for now; there will be another judgment."

sentences.zh: 」於是令曰：「廷尉執處侯剛，於法如猛。

translations.literal: She then issued: "The Judicial Court's handling of Hou Gang is, by the law, severe indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, she then issued: "The Judicial Court's handling of Hou Gang is, by the law, severe indeed.

sentences.zh: 剛既意在為公，未宜便依所執。

translations.literal: But since Gang intended to act on behalf of the public, it is not appropriate to follow that ruling at once.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, but since Gang intended to act on behalf of the public, it is not appropriate to follow that ruling at once.

sentences.zh: 但輕勦民命，理無全捨，可削封三百戶，解嘗食典御。

translations.literal: Still, he lightly destroyed a man's life, and by reason and law he cannot be wholly spared; his fief should be cut by three hundred households, and he should be relieved of the office of Director of Tasting Food."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, still, he lightly destroyed a man's life, and by reason and law he cannot be wholly spared; his fief should be cut by three hundred households, and he should be relieved of the office of Director of Tasting Food."

sentences.zh: 」[9]剛於是頗為失意。

translations.literal: Gang was therefore rather disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, gang was therefore rather disappointed.

sentences.zh: 剛自太和進食，遂為典御，歷兩都、三帝、二太后，將三十年，至此始解。

translations.literal: From Taihe onward, Gang had served as Director of Tasting Food through two capitals, three emperors, and two empress dowagers for nearly thirty years, and only now was he finally relieved of it.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, from Taihe onward, Gang had served as Director of Tasting Food through two capitals, three emperors, and two empress dowagers for nearly thirty years, and only now was he finally relieved of it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Not long after, he was added as Gentleman Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, not long after, he was added as Gentleman Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉元匡之廢也，太后訪代匡者，剛為太傅、清河王懌所舉，遂除車騎將軍，領御史中尉，常侍、衞尉如故。

translations.literal: When Yuan Kuang was removed as imperial censor, the empress dowager sought a replacement; Gang was recommended by Grand Tutor Prince Qinghe Yi and was appointed General of the Chariots and Horses, in charge of the imperial censorate, while remaining Gentleman Attendant and Minister of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Yuan Kuang was removed as imperial censor, the empress dowager sought a replacement; Gang was recommended by Grand Tutor Prince Qinghe Yi and was appointed General of the Chariots and Horses, in charge of the imperial censorate, while remaining Gentleman Attendant and Minister of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 及領軍元叉執政擅權，樹結親黨，剛長子，叉之妹夫，乃引剛為侍中、左衞將軍，[10]還領尚食典御，以為枝援。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha, commander of the guards, took over as ruler and wielded power, he built up his own faction; Gang's eldest son was Yuan Cha's brother-in-law, so Yuan Cha brought Gang in as Palace Attendant and Left Guard General, and again put him in charge of Director of Tasting Food as a branch support.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Yuan Cha, commander of the guards, took over as ruler and wielded power, he built up his own faction; Gang's eldest son was Yuan Cha's brother-in-law, so Yuan Cha brought Gang in as Palace Attendant and Left Guard General, and again put him in charge of Director of Tasting Food as a branch support.

sentences.zh: 俄加車騎大將軍、領左右，復前削之封。

translations.literal: Before long he was added as Grand General of the Chariots and Horses and commander of the left and right guards, and his earlier reduction of his fief was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, before long he was added as Grand General of the Chariots and Horses and commander of the left and right guards, and his earlier reduction of his fief was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋加儀同，復領御史中尉。

translations.literal: Soon he was also given the title of Peer-Equal official and again put in charge of the imperial censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, soon he was also given the title of Peer-Equal official and again put in charge of the imperial censorate.

sentences.zh: 剛啟軍旅稍興，國用不足，求以封邑俸粟賑給征人，肅宗許之。

translations.literal: Gang petitioned that the army was now gradually growing, but the state funds were insufficient, and asked to use the revenues and grain from his fief to supply the expeditionary troops; Emperor Suzong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, gang petitioned that the army was now gradually growing, but the state funds were insufficient, and asked to use the revenues and grain from his fief to supply the expeditionary troops; Emperor Suzong granted it.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年，除領軍，餘官如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang, he was appointed Commander of the Guards, while his other posts remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in the first year of Xiaochang, he was appointed Commander of the Guards, while his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初元叉之解領軍也，靈太后以叉腹心尚多，恐難卒制，故權以剛代之，示安其意。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha was first relieved of the command of the guards, the Empress Dowager knew that his inner clique was still numerous and feared he would be difficult to control at once, so she temporarily used Gang in his place to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Yuan Cha was first relieved of the command of the guards, the Empress Dowager knew that his inner clique was still numerous and feared he would be difficult to control at once, so she temporarily used Gang in his place to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 尋出為散騎常侍、冀州刺史、將軍、儀同三司。
