translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Gentleman Attendant of the Cavalry, Inspector of Jizhou, General, and Peer-Equal official.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, soon he was sent out as Gentleman Attendant of the Cavalry, Inspector of Jizhou, General, and Peer-Equal official.

sentences.zh: [11]剛行在道，詔曰：「剛因緣時會，恩隆自久，擢於凡品，越昇顯爵。

translations.literal: On Gang's way out, the edict said: "Gang, by fortunate timing and circumstance, has long enjoyed great favor and has been raised from the ranks of the common to lofty rank.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, on Gang's way out, the edict said: "Gang, by fortunate timing and circumstance, has long enjoyed great favor and has been raised from the ranks of the common to lofty rank.

sentences.zh: 往以微勤，賞同利建，寵靈之極，超絕夷等。

translations.literal: In the past, for small services he received the same reward as those who established the state, and the favor shown him was extreme, surpassing his peers.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in the past, for small services he received the same reward as those who established the state, and the favor shown him was extreme, surpassing his peers.

sentences.zh: 曾無犬馬識主之誠，方懷梟鏡返噬之志。

translations.literal: He has never shown even the loyalty of a dog or horse to recognize his lord, yet he now harbors the ambition of a hawk or mirror that turns to bite back.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he has never shown even the loyalty of a dog or horse to recognize his lord, yet he now harbors the ambition of a hawk or mirror that turns to bite back.

sentences.zh: 與權臣元叉婚姻朋黨，虧違典制，長直禁中，一出一入，迭為姦防。

translations.literal: He married into the powerful Yuan Cha clan and formed a party, violating established norms; he was long stationed in the inner palace, going in and out, and thereby became a source of corruption and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he married into the powerful Yuan Cha clan and formed a party, violating established norms; he was long stationed in the inner palace, going in and out, and thereby became a source of corruption and obstruction.

sentences.zh: 又與劉騰共為心膂，間隔二宮，逼脅內外。

translations.literal: He also joined with Liu Teng as a trusted confidant, separating the two palaces and oppressing both inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he also joined with Liu Teng as a trusted confidant, separating the two palaces and oppressing both inside and out.

sentences.zh: 且位居繩憲，糾察是司，宜立格言，勢同鷹隼。

translations.literal: And since he holds a position where the statutes should be enforced and inspections carried out, he should be a model of strict words, with a power like an eagle or falcon.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, and since he holds a position where the statutes should be enforced and inspections carried out, he should be a model of strict words, with a power like an eagle or falcon.

sentences.zh: 方嚴楚撻，枉服貞良，專任凶威，以直為曲。

translations.literal: Instead, he harshly beat the innocent and the upright into false confessions, and by relying on brutal force turned right into wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, instead, he harshly beat the innocent and the upright into false confessions, and by relying on brutal force turned right into wrong.

sentences.zh: 不忠不道，深暴民聽；

translations.literal: His disloyalty and lack of principle are openly and deeply heard by the people;
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, his disloyalty and lack of principle are openly and deeply heard by the people;

sentences.zh: 附下罔上，事彰幽顯。

translations.literal: his siding with the lower and deceiving the higher has been evident both in secret and in the open.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, his siding with the lower and deceiving the higher has been evident both in secret and in the open.

sentences.zh: 莫大之罪，難從宥原，封爵之科，理宜貶奪。

translations.literal: The greatest of crimes makes pardon difficult, and the penalties for rank and title should properly be reduced and stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the greatest of crimes makes pardon difficult, and the penalties for rank and title should properly be reduced and stripped.

sentences.zh: 可征虜將軍，餘悉削黜。

translations.literal: He should be reduced to General of the Conquering Barbarians, and all other offices stripped away and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he should be reduced to General of the Conquering Barbarians, and all other offices stripped away and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 」剛終于家。

translations.literal: Gang ended his life at home.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, gang ended his life at home.

sentences.zh: 永安中，贈司徒公。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era, he was posthumously granted the title of Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in the Yong'an era, he was posthumously granted the title of Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 剛長子詳，自奉朝請稍遷通直散騎侍郎、冠軍將軍、主衣都統。

translations.literal: Gang's eldest son, Xiang, started as an attendant at court and was gradually promoted to Gentleman Attendant of the Regular Audience, General of the Champion Guard, and Chief of the Household Clothing Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, gang's eldest son, Xiang, started as an attendant at court and was gradually promoted to Gentleman Attendant of the Regular Audience, General of the Champion Guard, and Chief of the Household Clothing Bureau.

sentences.zh: 剛以上谷先有侯氏，於是始家焉。

translations.literal: Because there had once been a Marquis of the Hou clan in Shanggu, Gang then settled his household there.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, because there had once been a Marquis of the Hou clan in Shanggu, Gang then settled his household there.

sentences.zh: 正光中，又請以詳為燕州刺史，將軍如故，欲為家世之基。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang period, he also requested that Xiang be made Inspector of Yanzhou, with the general title remaining unchanged, in order to establish the foundation of the family line.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in the Zhengguang period, he also requested that Xiang be made Inspector of Yanzhou, with the general title remaining unchanged, in order to establish the foundation of the family line.

sentences.zh: 尋進後將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to General of the Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, before long he was promoted to General of the Rear Guard.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜司徒左長史，領嘗藥典御、燕州大中正。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Left Chief Clerk to the Minister over the Masses and given charge of Director of Tasting Food and Grand Arbiter of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in the fifth year, he was appointed Left Chief Clerk to the Minister over the Masses and given charge of Director of Tasting Food and Grand Arbiter of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 興和中，驃騎將軍、殷州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era, he served as General of the Cavalry and Inspector of Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in the Xinghe era, he served as General of the Cavalry and Inspector of Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 還朝，久而卒。

translations.literal: After returning to court, he died after a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, after returning to court, he died after a long time.

sentences.zh: 鄭儼，字季然，滎陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yan, courtesy name Jiran, was a man of Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, zheng Yan, courtesy name Jiran, was a man of Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 容貌壯麗。

translations.literal: He was a handsome man.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was a handsome man.

sentences.zh: 初為司徒胡國珍行參軍，因緣為靈太后所幸，時人未之知也。

translations.literal: At first he served as acting army officer for Minister over the Masses Hu Guozhen, and through this connection won the favor of Empress Dowager Ling, though people at the time did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, at first he served as acting army officer for Minister over the Masses Hu Guozhen, and through this connection won the favor of Empress Dowager Ling, though people at the time did not know it.

sentences.zh: 遷員外散騎侍郎、直後。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Regular Audience without Concurrent Office and then to Director of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Regular Audience without Concurrent Office and then to Director of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 靈太后廢，蕭寶夤西征，以儼為開府屬。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling was deposed, and Xiao Baoyin marched west, Yan was appointed an aide in the Open Mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Empress Dowager Ling was deposed, and Xiao Baoyin marched west, Yan was appointed an aide in the Open Mansion.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，太后反政，儼請使還朝，復見寵待。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, when the empress dowager returned to power, Yan requested to be sent back to court and again won favor and treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, at the beginning of Xiaochang, when the empress dowager returned to power, Yan requested to be sent back to court and again won favor and treatment.

sentences.zh: 拜諫議大夫、中書舍人，領嘗食典御。

translations.literal: He was appointed Censorial Grandee, Secretariat Drafter, and given charge of Director of Tasting Food.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was appointed Censorial Grandee, Secretariat Drafter, and given charge of Director of Tasting Food.

sentences.zh: 晝夜禁中，寵愛尤甚。

translations.literal: Day and night within the forbidden palace, he was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, day and night within the forbidden palace, he was especially favored.

sentences.zh: 儼每休沐，太后常遣閹童隨侍，儼見其妻，唯得言家事而已。

translations.literal: Whenever Yan was off duty, the Empress Dowager would usually send eunuch boys to accompany him; when Yan saw his wife, he could only speak about household matters.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, whenever Yan was off duty, the Empress Dowager would usually send eunuch boys to accompany him; when Yan saw his wife, he could only speak about household matters.

sentences.zh: 與徐紇俱為舍人。

translations.literal: He served together with Xu He as a secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he served together with Xu He as a secretary.

sentences.zh: 儼以紇有智數，仗為謀主；

translations.literal: Yan relied on He's intelligence and strategy and took him as his chief planner;
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, yan relied on He's intelligence and strategy and took him as his chief planner;

sentences.zh: 紇以儼寵幸既盛，傾身承接。

translations.literal: He, seeing Yan's favored status grow ever greater, bent himself to accommodate and serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he, seeing Yan's favored status grow ever greater, bent himself to accommodate and serve him.

sentences.zh: 共相表裏，勢動內外。

translations.literal: The two complemented each other, and their influence moved both inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the two complemented each other, and their influence moved both inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 城陽王徽微與之合，當時政令歸於儼等。

translations.literal: Prince Chengyang Hui had a slight connection with them, and at the time policy and orders were controlled by Yan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, prince Chengyang Hui had a slight connection with them, and at the time policy and orders were controlled by Yan and the others.

sentences.zh: 遷通直郎、散騎常侍、平東將軍、武衞將軍、華林都將、右衞將軍、散騎常侍、中軍將軍、中書令、車騎將軍，舍人、常侍如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Regular Audience, Gentleman Attendant of the Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the East, General of the Martial Guard, Commander of Hualin, General of the Right Guard, Gentleman Attendant of the Cavalry, General of the Center Army, Secretariat Director, and General of the Chariot and Horse, while his posts as secretary and attendant remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Regular Audience, Gentleman Attendant of the Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the East, General of the Martial Guard, Commander of Hualin, General of the Right Guard, Gentleman Attendant of the Cavalry, General of the Center Army, Secretariat Director, and General of the Chariot and Horse, while his posts as secretary and attendant remained as before.

sentences.zh: 肅宗崩，事出倉卒，天下咸言儼計也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong died, the matter happened in great haste, and everyone under heaven said it had been Yan's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Emperor Suzong died, the matter happened in great haste, and everyone under heaven said it had been Yan's plan.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮舉兵向洛，以儼、紇為辭。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong raised troops toward Luoyang, using Yan and He as his pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, erzhu Rong raised troops toward Luoyang, using Yan and He as his pretext.

sentences.zh: 榮逼京師，儼走歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When Rong pressed on the capital, Yan fled back to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Rong pressed on the capital, Yan fled back to his native place.

sentences.zh: 儼從兄仲明先為滎陽太守，至是，儼與仲明欲據郡起眾。

translations.literal: Yan's cousin Zhongming had earlier been Inspector of Yingyang; now Yan and Zhongming wanted to seize the commandery and raise a following.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, yan's cousin Zhongming had earlier been Inspector of Yingyang; now Yan and Zhongming wanted to seize the commandery and raise a following.

sentences.zh: 尋為其部下所殺，與仲明俱傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: Soon he was killed by his own subordinates, and he and Zhongming were both sent to Luoyang as severed heads.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, soon he was killed by his own subordinates, and he and Zhongming were both sent to Luoyang as severed heads.

sentences.zh: 子文寬，從出帝歿關西。

translations.literal: His son Wenkuan accompanied Emperor Daowu's death in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, his son Wenkuan accompanied Emperor Daowu's death in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 徐紇，字武伯，樂安博昌人也。

translations.literal: Xu He, courtesy name Wubo, was a man of Bochang in Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, xu He, courtesy name Wubo, was a man of Bochang in Le'an.

sentences.zh: 家世寒微。

translations.literal: His family had long been poor and insignificant.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, his family had long been poor and insignificant.

sentences.zh: 紇少好學，有名理，頗以文詞見稱。

translations.literal: He loved learning from youth, had a reputation for clear reasoning, and was much praised for his writing.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he loved learning from youth, had a reputation for clear reasoning, and was much praised for his writing.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，對策上第，高祖拔為主書。

translations.literal: He was examined as Xiaolian, scored first in the policy examination, and Gaozu selected him as Chief Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was examined as Xiaolian, scored first in the policy examination, and Gaozu selected him as Chief Scribe.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，除中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he was appointed Secretariat Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, at the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he was appointed Secretariat Secretary.

sentences.zh: 諂附趙脩，遷通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He flattered and attached himself to Zhao Xiu, and was promoted to Gentleman Attendant of the Regular Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he flattered and attached himself to Zhao Xiu, and was promoted to Gentleman Attendant of the Regular Audience.

sentences.zh: 及脩誅，坐黨徙枹罕。

translations.literal: When Xiu was executed, he was implicated as a member of Xiu's faction and exiled to Buhan.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Xiu was executed, he was implicated as a member of Xiu's faction and exiled to Buhan.

sentences.zh: 雖在徒役，志氣不撓。

translations.literal: Though he was in penal labor, his spirit remained unbowed.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, though he was in penal labor, his spirit remained unbowed.

sentences.zh: 故事，捉逃役流兵五人，流者聽免，紇以此得還。

translations.literal: By custom, five fugitives captured from penal service would earn release for the exiles; He was therefore able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, by custom, five fugitives captured from penal service would earn release for the exiles; He was therefore able to return.

sentences.zh: 久之，復除中書舍人。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was again appointed Secretariat Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, after a long time, he was again appointed Secretariat Secretary.

sentences.zh: 太傅、清河王懌又以文翰待之。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor, Prince Qinghe Yi, also treated him for his literary ability.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the Grand Tutor, Prince Qinghe Yi, also treated him for his literary ability.

sentences.zh: 及領軍元叉之害懌也，出為雁門太守。

translations.literal: When Commander Yuan Cha harmed Yi, He was sent out as Administrator of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Commander Yuan Cha harmed Yi, He was sent out as Administrator of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 紇稱母老，解郡還鄉。

translations.literal: He claimed his mother was old, resigned the commandery, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he claimed his mother was old, resigned the commandery, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 至家未幾，尋入洛，飾貌事叉，大得叉意。

translations.literal: Not long after reaching home, he soon entered Luoyang, polished his appearance, and served Yuan Cha; Yuan Cha greatly approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, not long after reaching home, he soon entered Luoyang, polished his appearance, and served Yuan Cha; Yuan Cha greatly approved of him.

sentences.zh: 及叉父繼西鎮潼關，以紇為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha's father Ji went west to garrison Tong Pass, He was appointed Chief of the Staff Office.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Yuan Cha's father Ji went west to garrison Tong Pass, He was appointed Chief of the Staff Office.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Before long he returned home for mourning after his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, before long he returned home for mourning after his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，以紇曾為懌所顧待，復起為中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling took back power, because He had once been favored by Yi, he was again raised as Secretariat Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Empress Dowager Ling took back power, because He had once been favored by Yi, he was again raised as Secretariat Secretary.

sentences.zh: 紇又曲事鄭儼，是以特被信任。

translations.literal: He also served Zheng Yan with all sorts of flattery, and was therefore specially trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he also served Zheng Yan with all sorts of flattery, and was therefore specially trusted.

sentences.zh: 俄遷給事黃門侍郎，仍領舍人，總攝中書門下之事，軍國詔命，莫不由之。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, while still holding his post as secretary; he took overall charge of the affairs of the Secretariat and the Gate Department, and all military and state edicts passed through him.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, before long he was promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, while still holding his post as secretary; he took overall charge of the affairs of the Secretariat and the Gate Department, and all military and state edicts passed through him.

sentences.zh: 時有急速，令數友執筆，[12]或行或臥，人別占之，造次俱成，不失事理，雖無雅裁，亦可通情。

translations.literal: When matters were urgent, several friends were told to hold the pen,[12] and each, whether walking or lying down, was assigned a portion; in haste they all got it done without losing the point, and though it lacked elegance, it still conveyed the sense.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when matters were urgent, several friends were told to hold the pen,[12] and each, whether walking or lying down, was assigned a portion; in haste they all got it done without losing the point, and though it lacked elegance, it still conveyed the sense.

sentences.zh: 時黃門侍郎太原王遵業、琅雅王誦並稱文學，亦不免為紇秉筆，求其指授。

translations.literal: At the time, Assistant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Wang Zunye of Taiyuan and Wang Song of Langya were both famed for their learning, yet even they had to let He take the brush and ask for his guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, at the time, Assistant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Wang Zunye of Taiyuan and Wang Song of Langya were both famed for their learning, yet even they had to let He take the brush and ask for his guidance.

sentences.zh: 尋加鎮南將軍、金紫光祿大夫，黃門、舍人如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional titles of General Who Guards the South and Grand Master of the Golden Purple Radiance, while retaining his Yellow Gate and secretary posts.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, soon he was given the additional titles of General Who Guards the South and Grand Master of the Golden Purple Radiance, while retaining his Yellow Gate and secretary posts.

sentences.zh: 紇機辯有智數。

translations.literal: He was clever and quick with strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he was clever and quick with strategy.

sentences.zh: 當公斷決，終日不以為勞。

translations.literal: When handling official judgments, he could work all day without finding it tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when handling official judgments, he could work all day without finding it tiring.

sentences.zh: 長直禁中，略無休息。

translations.literal: He stayed almost constantly in the forbidden palace, with little rest.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, he stayed almost constantly in the forbidden palace, with little rest.

sentences.zh: 時復與沙門講論，或分宵達曙，而心力無怠，道俗歎服之。

translations.literal: At times he also debated with monks, sometimes talking from night until dawn, and his mind and strength never slackened; both clergy and laymen admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, at times he also debated with monks, sometimes talking from night until dawn, and his mind and strength never slackened; both clergy and laymen admired him.

sentences.zh: 然性浮動，慕權利，外似謇正，內實諂諛。

translations.literal: But by nature he was fickle and sought power and profit; outwardly he seemed honest and upright, but inwardly he was truly flattering and sycophantic.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, but by nature he was fickle and sought power and profit; outwardly he seemed honest and upright, but inwardly he was truly flattering and sycophantic.

sentences.zh: 時豪勝己，必相陵駕；

translations.literal: When someone of higher status was present, he would certainly try to outdo and suppress them;
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when someone of higher status was present, he would certainly try to outdo and suppress them;

sentences.zh: 書生貧士，矯意禮之。

translations.literal: when scholars or poor gentlemen were present, he deliberately lowered himself and was polite to them.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when scholars or poor gentlemen were present, he deliberately lowered himself and was polite to them.

sentences.zh: 其詭態若此，有識鄙薄焉。

translations.literal: Such were his hypocritical ways, and those with any discernment looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, such were his hypocritical ways, and those with any discernment looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 紇既處腹心，參斷機密，勢傾一時，遠近填湊。

translations.literal: Once He became a heart-and-liver confidant and took part in deciding secret matters, his influence overflowed for a time and people from near and far crowded around him.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, once He became a heart-and-liver confidant and took part in deciding secret matters, his influence overflowed for a time and people from near and far crowded around him.

sentences.zh: 與鄭儼、李神軌寵任相亞，時稱徐鄭焉。

translations.literal: His favor and responsibility were second only to Zheng Yan and Li Shengui, and people at the time spoke of "Xu and Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, his favor and responsibility were second only to Zheng Yan and Li Shengui, and people at the time spoke of "Xu and Zheng."

sentences.zh: 然無經國大體，好行小數，說靈太后以鐵券間尒朱榮左右，榮知，深以為憾，啟求誅之。

translations.literal: Yet he lacked a proper grasp of statecraft and preferred petty tricks; he told Empress Dowager Ling to use iron certificates to separate Erzhu Rong from the people around him, and when Rong learned of it, he took deep offense and asked that He be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, yet he lacked a proper grasp of statecraft and preferred petty tricks; he told Empress Dowager Ling to use iron certificates to separate Erzhu Rong from the people around him, and when Rong learned of it, he took deep offense and asked that He be killed.

sentences.zh: 榮將入洛，既克河梁，紇矯詔夜開殿門，取驊騮御馬十匹，東走兗州。

translations.literal: When Rong was about to enter Luoyang and had already taken the Heliang crossing, He forged an edict and opened the palace gates at night, took ten imperial horses from the famous Hualiu stable, and fled east to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when Rong was about to enter Luoyang and had already taken the Heliang crossing, He forged an edict and opened the palace gates at night, took ten imperial horses from the famous Hualiu stable, and fled east to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 紇弟獻伯為北海太守，獻伯弟季彥先為青州長史，紇使人告之，亦將家南走。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xianbo was then Inspector of Beihai, and his other younger brother Jiyan was Chief Clerk of Qingzhou; He sent messengers to tell them, and they too were going to flee south with the family.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, his younger brother Xianbo was then Inspector of Beihai, and his other younger brother Jiyan was Chief Clerk of Qingzhou; He sent messengers to tell them, and they too were going to flee south with the family.

sentences.zh: 羊侃時為太山太守，紇往投之，說侃令舉兵。

translations.literal: At the time, Yang Kan was Inspector of Taishan; He went to take refuge with him and urged him to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, at the time, Yang Kan was Inspector of Taishan; He went to take refuge with him and urged him to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 侃從之，遂聚兵反，共紇圍兗州。

translations.literal: Kan agreed, raised troops in rebellion, and together with He they surrounded Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, kan agreed, raised troops in rebellion, and together with He they surrounded Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，遣侍中于暉為行臺，與齊獻武王督諸軍討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, the palace attendant Yu Hui was sent as acting imperial commissioner, together with Emperor Wu of Qi to command the various armies against them.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, at the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, the palace attendant Yu Hui was sent as acting imperial commissioner, together with Emperor Wu of Qi to command the various armies against them.

sentences.zh: 紇慮不免，說侃請乞師於蕭衍。

translations.literal: Fearing he would not escape, He persuaded Kan to ask for aid from Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, fearing he would not escape, He persuaded Kan to ask for aid from Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 侃信之，遂奔衍。

translations.literal: Kan believed him and fled to Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, kan believed him and fled to Xiao.

sentences.zh: 文筆駁論數十卷，多有遺落，時或存於世焉。

translations.literal: His writings and arguments ran to several dozen volumes, but many have been lost, though some still survive today.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, his writings and arguments ran to several dozen volumes, but many have been lost, though some still survive today.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰。

translations.literal: The historiographer says.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the historiographer says.

translations.literal: 〈Gap〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Accordingly, 〈Gap〉〉

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, collation notes

sentences.zh: 都曹尚書曹百僚之首 按上稱「領都曹，為尚書令」，下稱「都曹尚書令可權記」。

translations.literal: The chief of the Capital Offices was the head of the hundred officials. The note says that the preceding line reads "in charge of the Capital Offices, serving as Secretary," and the line below reads "the chief of the Capital Offices, Secretary may be temporarily recorded."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the chief of the Capital Offices was the head of the hundred officials. The note says that the preceding line reads "in charge of the Capital Offices, serving as Secretary," and the line below reads "the chief of the Capital Offices, Secretary may be temporarily recorded."

sentences.zh: 這裏「尚書曹」疑當作尚書令。

translations.literal: Here, "Secretary" is probably meant to be "Secretary General."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, here, "Secretary" is probably meant to be "Secretary General."

sentences.zh: 語在常景傳 按今常景傳

translations.literal: The wording is in the biography of Chang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the wording is in the biography of Chang Jing.

sentences.zh: 〈卷八二〉

translations.literal: 〈Volume 82〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Accordingly, 〈Volume 82〉〉

sentences.zh: 以北史補，不載其事。

translations.literal: It is supplemented by the Northern History and does not record the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, it is supplemented by the Northern History and does not record the matter.

sentences.zh: 滋水沒川之彥 冊府卷五三０

translations.literal: Yan of Zishui who "submerged the river"; Cefu, volume 530
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, yan of Zishui who "submerged the river"; Cefu, volume 530

sentences.zh: 〈六三三四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 6334〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Accordingly, 〈Page 6334〉〉

sentences.zh: 「滋水沒川」作「丘樊林藪」。

translations.literal: "Zishui submerges the river" is written as "Qiu fan lin sou."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, "Zishui submerges the river" is written as "Qiu fan lin sou."

sentences.zh: 按「滋水沒川」未詳，或有訛字，冊府恐是以意改。

translations.literal: The phrase "Zishui submerges the river" is unclear; there may be a scribal error, and the Cefu version probably altered it by sense.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the phrase "Zishui submerges the river" is unclear; there may be a scribal error, and the Cefu version probably altered it by sense.

sentences.zh: 趙郡南欒人也 按卷一０六上地形志上，南欒屬南趙郡，「南」字不宜省。

translations.literal: A man of South Luan in Zhaojun. According to the Geography treatise in volume 106, upper, South Luan belonged to South Zhaojun, so the word "South" should not be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, a man of South Luan in Zhaojun. According to the Geography treatise in volume 106, upper, South Luan belonged to South Zhaojun, so the word "South" should not be omitted.

sentences.zh: 為齋帥 諸本「齋」作「齊」。

translations.literal: Zhai Shuai. In the various editions, "Zhai" is written as "Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, zhai Shuai. In the various editions, "Zhai" is written as "Qi."

sentences.zh: 按下文作「齋」，「齋帥」屢見本書，又見隋書卷二七百官志中。

translations.literal: The note says that below it is written "Zhai"; "Zhai Shuai" appears many times in this book and also in the Sui Shu, volume 27, Treatise on Offices, part 2.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the note says that below it is written "Zhai"; "Zhai Shuai" appears many times in this book and also in the Sui Shu, volume 27, Treatise on Offices, part 2.

sentences.zh: 「齊」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: The character "Qi" is a scribal error; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the character "Qi" is a scribal error; it is now corrected.

sentences.zh: 始琛及李憑等曲事於脩 諸本「憑」作「馮」。

translations.literal: In some editions, "Ping" is written as "Feng."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in some editions, "Ping" is written as "Feng."

sentences.zh: 按卷六八甄琛傳、通鑑卷一四五

translations.literal: The note says that in volume 68, the biography of Zhen Chen, and in the Zizhi Tongjian, volume 145, it is written as "Ping."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the note says that in volume 68, the biography of Zhen Chen, and in the Zizhi Tongjian, volume 145, it is written as "Ping."

sentences.zh: 〈四五三五頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 4535〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Accordingly, 〈Page 4535〉〉

sentences.zh: 作「憑」。

translations.literal: It is written as "Ping."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, it is written as "Ping."

sentences.zh: 「馮」即「憑」本字，今統一作「憑」。

translations.literal: "Feng" is the older form of "Ping"; here it has been standardized to "Ping."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, "Feng" is the older form of "Ping"; here it has been standardized to "Ping."

sentences.zh: 又有淫宴 北史卷九二茹皓附義恭傳「又」作「叉」，這裏「又」當是「叉」之訛。

translations.literal: In the Northern History, volume 92, in the attached biography of Ru Hao and Yi Gong, the word is "Cha" rather than "You"; here "You" must be a scribal error for "Cha."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in the Northern History, volume 92, in the attached biography of Ru Hao and Yi Gong, the word is "Cha" rather than "You"; here "You" must be a scribal error for "Cha."

sentences.zh: 其以剛為右衞大將軍 墓誌集釋侯剛墓誌

translations.literal: To appoint Gang as Grand General of the Right Guard. The epitaph collection says
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, to appoint Gang as Grand General of the Right Guard. The epitaph collection says

sentences.zh: 〈圖版二四九之二〉

translations.literal: 〈Plate 249, image 2〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Accordingly, 〈Plate 249, image 2〉〉

sentences.zh: 稱「延昌元年，進右衞將軍」。

translations.literal: It states: "In the first year of Yanchang, he was promoted to General of the Right Guard."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, it states: "In the first year of Yanchang, he was promoted to General of the Right Guard."

sentences.zh: 按此時左、右衞將軍不見加「大」之例，下文說「熙平中，除左衞將軍」，也不加「大」，這裏「大」字當衍。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Guard Generals are not otherwise given the word "Great" at this time; likewise below, when it says he was appointed General of the Left Guard in Xiaping, it does not include "Great." So the character "Great" here is probably extraneous.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the Left and Right Guard Generals are not otherwise given the word "Great" at this time; likewise below, when it says he was appointed General of the Left Guard in Xiaping, it does not include "Great." So the character "Great" here is probably extraneous.

sentences.zh: 解嘗食典御 諸本「嘗食」作「尚衣」，北史卷九二侯剛傳作「嘗食」。

translations.literal: Relieve him of the office of Director of Tasting Food. In various editions, "tasting food" is written as "clothing," but the Northern History, volume 92, biography of Hou Gang, has "tasting food."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, relieve him of the office of Director of Tasting Food. In various editions, "tasting food" is written as "clothing," but the Northern History, volume 92, biography of Hou Gang, has "tasting food."

sentences.zh: 張森楷云：「按前文剛只為嘗食典御，未嘗為尚衣，疑『尚衣』訛。

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai says: "Looking at the previous text, Gang only ever served as Director of Tasting Food and never as Director of Clothing; I suspect 'clothing' is a scribal error."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, zhang Senkai says: "Looking at the previous text, Gang only ever served as Director of Tasting Food and never as Director of Clothing; I suspect 'clothing' is a scribal error."

sentences.zh: 」按侯剛本以善於烹調進用，下文說他「自太和進食，遂為典御，

translations.literal: Looking at Hou Gang's biography, he was originally promoted because he was good at cooking; below
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, looking at Hou Gang's biography, he was originally promoted because he was good at cooking; below

sentences.zh: 〈中略〉

translations.literal: 〈omitted〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Accordingly, 〈omitted〉〉

sentences.zh: 至此始解」。

translations.literal: At this point, he was only then relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, at this point, he was only then relieved.

sentences.zh: 這裏作「尚衣」誤，今據北史改。

translations.literal: Here, writing "clothing" is an error; it is corrected here according to the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, here, writing "clothing" is an error; it is corrected here according to the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 乃引剛為侍中左衞將軍 墓誌集釋

translations.literal: To bring Gang in as Palace Attendant and Left Guard General. The epitaph collection
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, to bring Gang in as Palace Attendant and Left Guard General. The epitaph collection

sentences.zh: 〈圖版二四九之二〉

translations.literal: 〈Plate 249, image 2〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Accordingly, 〈Plate 249, image 2〉〉

sentences.zh: 稱「入居常伯，還領禁戎」，即指此次除授，集釋卷五以墓誌前文「延昌元年，進右衞將軍」當之，實誤，但引正光六年劉根造象，剛結銜作「右衞將軍」，證這裏「左衞」為「右衞」之訛，疑是。

translations.literal: States: "Entering office as a regular attendant and again in charge of the palace guards," meaning this appointment. The collection, volume 5, takes the epitaph's earlier line "In the first year of Yanchang, he was promoted to General of the Right Guard" as the equivalent, which is actually mistaken; but an image inscription made in the sixth year of Zhengguang shows Gang's full title as "General of the Right Guard," proving that here "Left Guard" is likely a scribal error.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, states: "Entering office as a regular attendant and again in charge of the palace guards," meaning this appointment. The collection, volume 5, takes the epitaph's earlier line "In the first year of Yanchang, he was promoted to General of the Right Guard" as the equivalent, which is actually mistaken; but an image inscription made in the sixth year of Zhengguang shows Gang's full title as "General of the Right Guard," proving that here "Left Guard" is likely a scribal error.

sentences.zh: 將軍儀同三司 按「將軍」上無軍號。

translations.literal: General and Peer-Equal official. There is no army designation before "general."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, general and Peer-Equal official. There is no army designation before "general."

sentences.zh: 據上文稱「俄加車騎大將軍」，又云「尋加儀同」，疑本作「將軍、儀同如故」，後人改「如故」為「三司」。

translations.literal: Since earlier it says "He was soon added as Grand General of the Chariots and Horses," and then says "soon added as Peer-Equal," this probably originally read "general and peer-equal as before," with later scribes changing "as before" into "three offices."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, since earlier it says "He was soon added as Grand General of the Chariots and Horses," and then says "soon added as Peer-Equal," this probably originally read "general and peer-equal as before," with later scribes changing "as before" into "three offices."
